patch.summary: Update the workspace's Link tunnel access consent settings
patch.description: Set which callers may reach a Link (mablnet) tunnel owned by this workspace. Only settings present in the request are applied; omitted ones keep their current value, and an absent setting has always meant not consented. Available only to a workspace owner — deliberately not to global admins or api keys, since this is the customer's consent to give. Returns the updated workspace.

parameters.description: Organization id

put.summary: Update the workspace agent behavior settings, available only to workspace owners
put.description: Update all owner-managed agent behavior settings for the workspace in a single call. `require_agent_edits_on_branches` and `recovery_agent_auto_edits` are gated by the agentic_test_editing feature; if the workspace does not have that feature their values are ignored.

parameters.name: id

put.summary: Pin where the workspace's test runs execute
put.description: Pins the cloud and region that test runs of this workspace execute in. A pin on a workspace wins over one on its account, which wins over one on its company. A run whose test type does not execute in the pinned location runs in the default one. Only mabl can set it (global organizations write scope or mabl global admin).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the workspace

delete.summary: Remove the workspace's execution location pin
delete.description: Removes the workspace's pin, so its test runs follow the next pin up, or the default location. Same authorization as setting it.

parameters.name: id

put.summary: Update the workspace credential policy, available only to workspace owners
put.description: Update the workspace's credential policy. When `require_cloud_only_credentials` is true, credentials created in this workspace must be cloud credentials, and a create that does not ask for one is rejected. The policy is deliberately owner-managed rather than left to whoever creates the credential, and it applies to every caller including API keys. It governs creation only: credentials that already exist are neither converted nor made read-only.

get.description:
Retrieve the count of test runs in an active workspace, aggregated into time buckets. Each bucket reports the total number of runs that started within the bucket window, as well as how many of those passed and how many failed or were terminated. Useful for plotting test activity over time, tracking reliability trends, and feeding external dashboards with per-day/week/month usage metrics.

Runs are counted by their `start_time`, not `end_time` — a long-running test that starts on day D and finishes on day D+1 is attributed to day D. In-flight runs (ones that have started but not yet completed) are included in `total_test_runs` and counted as `failed_test_runs` until they complete, since they have not yet succeeded.

Optional filters (`application_id`, `plan_id`, `test_type`) narrow the underlying row set. Optional `group_by` (`plan` or `application`) breaks each time bucket further into one bucket per group value, with the `group_id` field on each bucket identifying the dimension value.

All timestamps in requests and responses are Unix epoch milliseconds. Bucket boundaries are aligned to UTC; convert to local time on the client side if needed. Time range is capped by granularity: daily (90 days), weekly/monthly (400 days). Data is served live from the test run database, so results reflect runs completed within seconds of the request.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The workspace ID

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive start of the time range to report on, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be strictly less than `end_time`.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Exclusive end of the time range to report on, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be strictly greater than `start_time`. The total window `end_time - start_time` is capped by granularity: 90 days for `daily`, 400 days for `weekly` or `monthly`. Requests exceeding the cap return HTTP 400.

parameters.name: granularity
parameters.description: Time bucket size for the response. Valid values are `daily`, `weekly`, and `monthly`. Daily buckets start at midnight UTC. Weekly buckets follow ISO-8601 week boundaries (Monday 00:00 UTC). Monthly buckets align with the first day of each calendar month at 00:00 UTC.

parameters.name: group_by
parameters.description: Optional dimension to break the response down by. Without `group_by`, each time bucket aggregates all matching runs. With `group_by` set, each time bucket is further split by the grouping value and the `group_id` field on each bucket identifies which plan, application, or workspace it represents (workspace only appears on account-level endpoints). Buckets are emitted for every (period, group_id) combination that has at least one matching run; combinations with zero runs are omitted.

parameters.name: application_id
parameters.description: Filter results to runs associated with a specific mabl application. Only runs whose `application_id` matches this value exactly are included. Combined additively with other filters (`plan_id`, `test_type`) — runs must match all provided filters.

parameters.name: plan_id
parameters.description: Filter results to runs that were part of executions of a specific test plan. Useful for attributing usage to a particular CI pipeline, schedule, or deployment trigger. Runs not associated with any plan (for example, ad-hoc runs from the Trainer) are excluded when this filter is set.

parameters.name: test_type
parameters.description: Filter results to runs of a specific test type. Valid values are `browser` (UI automation), `api` (REST API tests), `mobile`, and `performance`. Useful when a workspace exercises multiple test types and you want to report on them independently — for example, to split UI-automation usage from API-test usage in an attribution dashboard. When omitted, all test types are included.

200.description: Test run counts grouped by time buckets

get.description:
Same as `/workspaces/{workspace_id}/reports/usage/testRunCounts` but aggregates across every active workspace the authenticated caller has access to within the account. Use this endpoint for account-wide usage dashboards where you want a single aggregated bucket per time period, or pair it with `group_by=workspace` to produce a per-workspace breakdown of test run counts.

To scope the query to a single workspace within the account (for example, to reuse the same account-level API key while drilling into one workspace), pass its identifier as the `workspace_id` query parameter. When `workspace_id` is provided, the caller must still have access to that workspace.

All filter (`application_id`, `plan_id`, `test_type`), granularity, `group_by`, and time-range rules are identical to the workspace-level endpoint. All timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds.

get.description:
Retrieve total execution time for an active workspace, aggregated into time buckets. The `total_execution_seconds` field sums (end_time - start_time) across every completed run whose `start_time` falls within the bucket. In-flight runs (without a recorded end_time) are excluded both from this sum and from the `total_test_runs` count on this endpoint — consult `testRunCounts` if you want a count that includes in-flight runs.

Execution time is measured from the moment a run starts executing to the moment it completes (successfully or otherwise). It does not include time spent queued waiting for a runner. Useful for billing, capacity planning, or attributing compute cost to a specific team (via `application_id` or `plan_id`), test type, or time window.

All filter, granularity, and `group_by` semantics are identical to the `testRunCounts` endpoint. All timestamps are Unix epoch milliseconds, and bucket boundaries are aligned to UTC.

get.summary: Query workspace daily maximum concurrent test runs
get.description:
Retrieve the daily maximum number of simultaneously executing test runs in an active workspace, along with the workspace's configured test run concurrency limit for the same test type. The reported `max_test_run_concurrency` is computed as the maximum number of runs executing at any single instant during the day — not an average, not a count of runs started. If ten runs start and finish within the same minute but a different run was also executing for that minute, the maximum for that minute is eleven.

Use this endpoint to track how close a workspace is running to its purchased concurrency capacity, decide when to request a limit increase, identify load bursts, or correlate peak usage with customer-side deployment or traffic patterns. Compare the `max_test_run_concurrency` values against `configured_test_run_concurrency_limit` to see headroom.

Data is pre-aggregated from billable events by a background job that runs every 12 hours, so values for the current calendar day may be incomplete until the next aggregation cycle finishes. Time range cannot exceed 90 days. If `start_time` and `end_time` are both omitted, the endpoint returns the last 90 completed days ending at the start of the current UTC day.

The `configured_test_run_concurrency_limit` is resolved against the requested `test_type`. For `browser` (the default when unspecified), it is the sum of the workspace's Linux, macOS, and Windows browser quotas. For `api`, `mobile`, or `performance`, it is the single numeric quota for that resource. A workspace with no configured quota for a given test type returns `configured_test_run_concurrency_limit: 0`.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The workspace ID

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Inclusive start of the time range to report on, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be earlier than `end_time`. Optional: if both `start_time` and `end_time` are omitted, the endpoint returns the most recent 90 completed days. If `end_time` is provided but `start_time` is not, `start_time` defaults to 90 days before `end_time`. Any sub-day precision is snapped to midnight UTC of that day; the response echoes the snapped value.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: Exclusive end of the time range to report on, as Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be later than `start_time`. Optional: defaults to the start of the current calendar day in UTC (i.e. the end of the most recent completed day). The window `end_time - start_time` cannot exceed 90 days. Any sub-day precision is snapped to the start of the following UTC day; the response echoes the snapped value.

parameters.name: test_type
parameters.description: Test type to report maximum test run concurrency for. Valid values are `browser` (UI automation), `api` (REST API tests), `mobile`, and `performance`. The returned `max_test_run_concurrency` values and the matching `configured_test_run_concurrency_limit` both reflect the selected test type. Defaults to `browser` when omitted.

200.description: Daily maximum concurrent test run data for the workspace

post.summary: Search active test references by full-text token query.
post.description:
Token-based full-text search over a workspace's active tests, using the Spanner
SEARCH() function. A test is matched on its own name, description, intent, and
labels through `idx_test_reference_search_v2`; the default "combined" search covers
all four at once, and restricting `search_field` scopes the match to that one
column. The combined search also matches on the step text of a test's flows,
through `idx_flow_reference_search_v3`, so a test whose steps describe the query is
found even when its own name, description, intent and labels say nothing about it.
Step matches rank below every metadata match rather than competing with them; see
`match_source` for the tier rule.

Returns rich per-test rows, including an excerpt of the annotated step descriptions
of the test's flows (joined through `test_reference.flows` -> `flow_reference`).
Under the "combined" search a flow whose steps matched contributes a window of its
step text around the matching steps, a flow that did not match contributes its
opening steps, and the flows are ordered most relevant first, so that a capped
excerpt keeps the steps the query was about rather than whichever flows happen to
run first. Shaping the excerpt decides only which steps a row shows: it never
admits a test, and never changes how the returned tests rank.

The `query` follows Spanner search syntax — multi-token queries default to AND.
Callers can join keywords with " OR " for broader recall, or quote phrases.
`OR` binds only the two words beside it and parentheses do not group terms, so
prefer one plain multi-word query (all words required) over mixing `OR` with
other terms.

parameters.description: The workspace to search in.

200.description: Search results ordered by relevance score (descending).

post.description: Returns the most recent Xray sync AsynchronousJob for each requested plan's latest plan run, keyed by plan_id. Unlike a plan-run-keyed lookup this resolves the latest run server-side, so a plan whose last run was up to 400 days ago still reports its sync outcome. Latest-run resolution sees completed runs only and is updated asynchronously, so shortly after a run finishes this may still report the previous run — each status carries the plan_run_id its job belongs to.

post.summary: Re-validate the credentials stored in a TestRail integration
post.description: Validates the credentials stored in the given TestRail workspace integration against the live TestRail instance and returns the projects and required result fields visible to the credentialed user. The TestRail API key is write-only and never returned by the API, so this is how an existing integration is re-checked without the caller possessing the key. The response never includes the key.

parameters.name: workspace_integration_id
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the TestRail workspace integration to validate

get.summary: TestRail project and suites behind an integration
get.description: The integration's configured project (with its suite mode), the suites in that project, and the configured suite when there is one. Read-only against TestRail with the integration's stored credentials; lets a reader scope a case search without integration-write permission.

get.summary: Search TestRail cases behind an integration
get.description: One page of cases in the integration's project, scoped to its configured suite (or the requested suite when none is configured). A query that looks like a case id (digits, optionally prefixed with C) resolves that case and returns it only if it lies inside the same scope; any other query filters titles. Results are read live from TestRail; nothing is cached.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Case id or title text. Omitted lists the scope from the offset.

parameters.name: suite_id
parameters.description: Suite to search when the integration configures none (required then for multi-suite projects). Must equal the configured suite when there is one.

post.summary: Read the content of TestRail cases for use as a test-generation specification
post.description: Returns what each case actually specifies -- preconditions, steps, expected results -- normalised so the caller sees one structure whatever template the case uses. Unlike the lookup, which searches every enabled integration in the workspace, this names one: the integration must belong to this workspace and be enabled, and each case must lie inside its configured project and suite. Only fields on a fixed readable set are returned, because an instance may define text fields holding anything and this content is intended for a model. A case whose content lies entirely outside that set is reported no_readable_content rather than returned empty.

200.description: One entry per requested link, in request order

post.summary: Resolve a test's case links against the workspace's TestRail integrations
post.description: Classifies each link by shape and, for TestRail-shaped ones, asks every enabled TestRail integration in the workspace in a fixed order until one knows the case. A link is unknown_case only when every reachable integration rejected it; unavailable when none knew it and at least one could not be asked. Links that belong to another system (Jira keys, Zephyr case keys) are reported as other_platform without contacting TestRail.

200.description: One entry per requested link, in request order

post.summary: Read the content of Zephyr test cases for use as a test-generation specification
post.description: Returns what each case specifies -- objective, precondition, labels, and its steps or script -- for a model to read. The integration must belong to this workspace and be enabled, and each case's project must be one of its project_keys; a case outside them is out_of_scope without asking Zephyr. A step that calls another case is replaced by that case's steps, one level deep. Only a fixed set of fields is returned, because this content is intended for a model.

get.summary: Get signed URLs for the browser state a plan run's tests share
get.description:
Returns the signed URLs a test runner needs to read and write browser state that the
tests of one plan run share.

The state belongs to the plan run, and there is one per session scope — the application
origin plus the credentials. A flow plays no part in addressing it, and deliberately so:
the session is what decides reuse. A test that finds state for its session starts from it,
without comparing its marked flows against whatever the producing test had marked.

A marked flow still runs every time. It is not skipped, so it must decide for itself
whether there is anything left to do — a login flow, for example, wraps its sign-in steps
in a condition that only holds when the login page is actually showing. Leaving that
judgment to the flow is what makes reuse safe: a test can never miss a flow's effect
because some other test produced the state.

`signed_upload_url` is always present. `signed_download_url` is present only when state has
already been stored for this plan run and session scope, so its absence tells a runner to
run the flow itself. Runners that start together can all see no download URL and all
produce, and the write is unconditional, so the last one to upload wins — deliberately,
since a runner that finds an expired session has to be able to replace it. Answering both
questions in one response keeps a miss to the same number of round trips as a hit.

The workspace, and therefore the bucket, is derived server-side from the plan run, and the
object key is composed here from the plan run, the application origin and the
credentials. The caller supplies no path and learns no bucket name, so the URLs cannot be
steered at an unrelated object, and state is only ever shared between tests that would have
logged in as the same user against the same application.

The stored state belongs to the plan run and is never addressable by a later one, since
the key carries the plan run ID. It is not deleted when the run ends; it expires with the
workspace's stored test artifacts, and sooner where a shorter rule applies.

get.summary: Get the current mablnet peer-CA trust bundle for a link infrastructure cluster
get.description:
Returns the publisher-signed envelope carrying the X.509 root certificate(s) every mablnet client trusts as peer-CA roots when verifying mabl-side Host certs during the peer-to-peer QUIC TLS handshake. One bundle per link infrastructure cluster: the shared cluster's unless `infrastructure_key` names a dedicated one, and the same bundle for every caller asking for that cluster. A dedicated cluster's envelope carries its key in a signed `cluster` field, which a caller must check against the key it asked for; the shared cluster's has none. Bundle bytes come from the cluster's published trust bundle — the same anchors its Link Routers load on startup. More than one anchor may be present: a root rotation publishes the incoming anchor alongside the outgoing one, and callers should trust every certificate in the envelope.
The anchors are **non-secret** — X.509 root certificates are public artefacts by definition; protection here is integrity, not confidentiality. Auth is required for attribution / rate-limiting / audit, not because the bytes are sensitive. Integrity is what the envelope provides, and it is the only thing that makes these anchors safe to fetch: a caller must verify the signature against a publisher key it already holds, and must not accept anchors from anywhere else in this response.
Conditional refetch: callers send their last-known ETag as `If-None-Match` on each poll. The server returns `304 Not Modified` (no body) when the bundle is unchanged. The current ETag is mirrored in both the standard `ETag` header and the mabl-specific `x-mabl-entity-version` header (the latter survives upstream gzip-Vary stripping).

parameters.name: infrastructure_key
parameters.description: Link infrastructure key of the cluster whose bundle to return, as reported by `link_infrastructure_key` on the Link Agent or `infrastructure_key` on a resolved tunnel. Omit it, or pass `mabl`, for the shared cluster.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Last ETag the caller observed; server returns 304 when current ETag matches.

200.description: Current bundle returned in body; current ETag in headers.

ETag.description: Content-derived version of the bundle (SHA-256 hex of the published envelope bytes).

x-mabl-entity-version.description: Mirror of ETag; survives upstream gzip stripping.

304.description: Bundle unchanged since the supplied If-None-Match. Empty body; ETag headers still present.

404.description: No trust bundle is published for this deployment or cluster — the environment is not configured for mablnet, the cluster does not exist, or its bundle has not been written yet. Distinguish this from a mistyped path by the error body. Deliberately not a 5xx: the server is up and answering, and 503 is a status the proxies in front of the api own.

429.description: Too many bundles for dedicated clusters this server has not loaded yet were requested at once. Retry after the `Retry-After` header; this does not mean the cluster has no bundle.

post.summary: Authorize a mablnet Host to join a Link Label's tunnel
post.description:
Validates a `HostCredentials` blob presented by a mablnet client (Link Agent, execution Host, or future desktop-app Host) and returns the `tenantId` / `hostIdentity` / `validUntil` triple the mablnet protocol needs to admit the client. Internally called by Link Router on every carrier-join — see `mablnet-client-authorization.md in link/mablnet/docs` for the full design.
Three caller types are accepted, all auth'd against the standard mabl-api chain: `link_agent` API keys (workspace-scoped Link Agent keys), `execution` API keys (workspace-scoped, TTL'd, minted per test run), or user OAuth tokens (workspace members with write permission, mabl support admins included). The request body's `workspace_id` is cross-checked against the auth principal.
Failure semantics: `401` for bad credential / malformed body / stale `issued_at` / replayed `nonce` / (link_agent callers only) `host_id` not matching any active Link Agent; `402` for billing-suspended or LINK feature disabled; `403` for auth principal not authorised on `workspace_id`; `404` for a workspace that does not exist; `5xx` for transient backend failures including Redis-unavailable (fail-closed on the nonce cache).

requestBody.description: HostCredentials blob the client presented at carrier-join

402.description: Credential is valid but the workspace is billing-suspended or the LINK feature is disabled — the customer-facing churn signal Link Tunnel uses today.

404.description: The tunnel's workspace does not exist.

post.summary: Mint a tenant-scoped mablnet operator session (peer JOIN credential + operator-command token)
post.description:
Issues two short-lived signed artifacts the calling user needs to drive a mablnet operator session against a specific customer workspace:
1. A `peer_credential` — an Ed25519-signed blob the operator presents at JOIN time to be admitted as a peer in the customer's tenant. The api's `/authorize/host` endpoint recognises `role: "peer"` and validates the signature in lieu of an api_key check.
2. An `operator_token` — an Ed25519-signed blob carried per-request in `OperatorCommand.token`. The customer Host's `MablOperatorAuthorizer` validates the signature, checks the embedded `workspace_id` matches the Host's own workspace, and verifies the requested capability's required scope is in the granted scope list.
Both artifacts bind to one customer workspace (the `workspace_id` request parameter) so a leaked credential cannot cross tenant boundaries. The mabl-deployment private key is held in Cloud KMS; the api never sees the bytes. For operating on the Router fleet itself (not a customer Host), use `/authorize/operator/fleet`.
Auth: user-OAuth callers only — operator tokens are an interactive support / engineering capability, not a workspace-scoped API. Requires **both** the mabl support-admin claim **and** access to the tunnel, because the two answer different questions. Tunnel access — a user who can modify the workspace (owner, editor, or a support admin where the workspace has enabled Support Access), a company member for a company-owned tunnel, or the owner of a personal tunnel — is what `/authorize/peer` asks on its own, since minting a peer credential for test training is ordinary. The token minted here instead carries `drain:host`, carrier recycle/disconnect and fault injection, so consent gates the reach and the support-admin role gates the capability. The mabl global-admin claim administers mabl's own resources and grants nothing here.
Scope policy: every admitted caller gets the whole tenant scope catalog — every `read:*`, `probe:destination`, the `recycle:carrier` / `disconnect:carrier` / `drain:host` mutations, and the diagnostic + fault-injection `start:*` / `stop:*` activities. Reaching the tunnel is the access control; there is no tier behind it. Callers do not request scopes — the api decides.
Lifetime: 30 minutes per issued session; callers re-fetch when needed.

requestBody.description: Operator session parameters (the customer workspace to operate on).

403.description: Caller is authenticated but is not authorized for the requested tunnel — not a mabl support admin, or the tunnel's owner has not granted them access.

404.description: The requested workspace does not exist.

post.summary: Mint a fleet-scoped mablnet operator session (peer JOIN credential + operator-command token)
post.description:
Issues the same pair of short-lived signed artifacts as `/authorize/operator/tenant`, but for a **fleet** operator session — one that operates on the Link Router fleet itself (Router inventory, drain a Router) rather than a customer Host.
Both artifacts bind to the fleet sentinel workspace (`mabl`) rather than a customer workspace. The `peer_credential` is recognised locally by a Router's `OperatorTenantAuthenticator` (verified against the same KMS-held Ed25519 key, never resolved against a customer tunnel) and admits the operator to the Router's operator tenant; the `operator_token` carries the fleet scope set and is validated by the Router's `MablFleetOperatorAuthorizer`.
Auth: user-OAuth callers who are mabl **global admins only**. Fleet operations act across customers, so the support-admin diagnostic tier admitted by the tenant endpoint is deliberately excluded here.
Scope policy: global admins get the fleet scope set (`read:router-inventory`, `drain:router`, `write:log-level`). Callers do not request scopes — the api decides.
Lifetime: 30 minutes per issued session; callers re-fetch when needed.

requestBody.description: Fleet operator session parameters (audit label only; binds to the fleet sentinel workspace).

403.description: Caller is authenticated but is not a mabl global admin.

post.summary: Mint a mablnet peer JOIN credential for an OAuth-authenticated user
post.description:
Issues a single short-lived signed `peer_credential` the calling user presents at JOIN time to be admitted as a peer in a customer tenant. Unlike `/authorize/operator/tenant`, no operator-command token is minted — callers using this endpoint dial the customer's services (e.g., `socks5` for test training) as regular intra-tenant peers; no operator-interface capabilities are involved.
Auth: user-OAuth callers entitled to the tunnel's owner. For a workspace owner, a user with write access to the workspace — customer workspace members training against the workspace's SOCKS5 service, and mabl support admins where the workspace has enabled Support Access. For a company owner, a company admin or any member of the company; there is no standalone mabl global / support admin grant, because no company-level consent flag exists yet to gate one. For a user owner, that user alone.
Lifetime: 30 minutes per issued credential. To keep a longer session alive without changing the bound Host identity, refresh by re-minting with the prior credential's `host_id`.

requestBody.description: Peer credential parameters (the customer workspace to JOIN).

get.summary: Resolve the current mablnet worker manifest for the calling Host's channel
get.description:
Returns the signed release manifest the calling Host should run, after applying the channel's staged-rollout decision for this Host. The manifest body is an opaque, Ed25519-signed document (see `manifest-format.md in link/mablnet/docs`); the api stores and returns it without altering field *values*, so the consumer's JCS re-canonicalisation still verifies — see `link/mablnet/docs/deployment/release-pipeline-api.md` § Opaque signed documents. Rollout resolution (which version this Host receives) is computed server-side from the per-channel rollout state plus a stable per-Host bucket — see § Manifest resolution.
Conditional refetch: callers send their last-known ETag as `If-None-Match`; the server returns `304 Not Modified` (no body) when the resolved manifest is unchanged. The current ETag is mirrored in both the `ETag` header and the mabl-specific `x-mabl-entity-version` header.

parameters.name: artifact
parameters.description: Release artifact the channel belongs to: `mablnet-host` (the worker binary) or `link-agent` (the Java Link Agent bundle). Channels are namespaced per artifact, so `stable` for one artifact is unrelated to `stable` for another.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.description: Release channel to resolve against, within the artifact. The well-known channels are `latest` (newest main build — dev/non-prod) and `stable` (tag-promoted release — prod); ephemeral per-branch channels named for the branch (sanitised to `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, as the release workflows publish them) are also accepted, as is a major-version channel such as `3` for the Link Agent. get.summary: Resolve the mablnet tunnel target for an owner + label
get.description:
Resolves which mablnet tunnel to reach for a given `label`, and where (the mablnet WSS Router endpoint + whether a live agent is serving it). Two modes:
**Run resolution (default, `owner_type` omitted).** The cloud-test-run path: a test executor knows the run's `workspace_id` and the configured label but not the tunnel's owner. A company-owned tunnel `(company, label)` with a live agent wins, so standing up a company tunnel under a workspace tunnel's label moves that workspace onto it with no environment change, and stopping the company agent moves it back. Otherwise a workspace-owned tunnel `(workspace_id, label)` is returned, live or not (so the caller fails the run rather than silently routing elsewhere); otherwise the company tunnel with no live agent, if one exists. `404` when neither exists. A workspace that needs its own tunnel must use a label its company does not also use. (Company tunnels carry no `workspace_id`, so the workspace agent listing cannot find them — this is why the endpoint encapsulates the resolution.)
**Owner-aware (`owner_type` set).** Resolves the tunnel for an explicit owner — used by user-facing tooling (`mabl link-agents test …`) to reach a `user` (personal) or an explicit `company` tunnel. `owner_id` is required for `company`/`workspace`; for `user` it must be the caller's own id (a personal tunnel is private to its owner). Authorized like `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/peer`: a `user` owner only by that user, a `company` owner by a company admin/member, a `workspace` owner by a user who can modify it. `404` when no such tunnel exists.
`has_live_agent` reports whether a `ready` Link Agent advertising `mablnet_wss` has heartbeated within the liveness window for the resolved owner — the caller's pre-run "is this tunnel serviceable" gate, mirroring the legacy Link Server check.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: Run-resolution mode (`owner_type` omitted): the run's workspace, from which its company is derived. Required in this mode; ignored when `owner_type` is set.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Tunnel (Link Label) configured on the run's environment.

parameters.name: owner_type
parameters.description: Owner-aware mode: the kind of owner to resolve the tunnel for. Omit for the default run resolution.

parameters.name: owner_id
parameters.description: Owner-aware mode: the owner's id. Required when `owner_type` is `company` or `workspace`; for `user` it must be the caller's own user id (a personal tunnel is private to its owner).

404.description: No resolvable mablnet tunnel for that workspace + label — either no tunnel (workspace- or company-owned) exists, or the owner's cluster publishes no carrier endpoint. Both answer 404 deliberately: a status that distinguished them would tell an unauthorized caller which labels exist.

post.summary: Place Link Agent into maintenance mode
post.description: Place a Link Agent into maintenance mode. mabl-side routing immediately stops treating the Agent as an active target — legacy Link Servers no longer dispatch new requests to it, and the Agent's mablnet Host begins draining its carriers (refusing new streams while continuing to service in-flight ones). If `drain_timeout_seconds` is supplied, the Agent stops waiting for natural drain after that interval and moves to `drained` regardless; without a timeout it waits indefinitely. The Agent does not auto-shutdown — the final shutdown is left to whatever external orchestrator initiated the maintenance window (use `POST .../terminate` to stop it, or `DELETE` this resource to return it to service). post.description: Name-based resolution of a concept name to a knowledge graph node: (1) exact lowercased name + label match, (2) substring match via SEARCH_SUBSTRING on name_substring_tokens. Returns null when neither produces a match. The two are NOT equivalent: an exact match is a deterministic identity, while a substring match is a lexical name-overlap SIGNAL (match_kind name_substring) that the caller surfaces to its agent as a candidate to weigh, not an identity verdict. Semantic similarity is not performed here; use the similarityNeighbors endpoint for embedding-based neighborhood lookup. Writer-only endpoint (AMA uses this; not for general-purpose search). concept_type is restricted to Page, Workflow, Feature (AMA's writable concept labels).

200.description: A node matched by exact name+label (a deterministic identity) or by name substring (a lexical name-overlap signal for the caller's agent to weigh).

204.description: No node matched either resolution tier. Generated clients should treat this as a "no match" outcome (no response body).

post.summary: Find nearest-neighbor concepts to a candidate
post.description:
Returns the top-K active concept nodes most similar to a candidate concept by symmetric cosine similarity over the node embedding column. The App Modeling Agent uses this to see the nearest existing concepts when resolving a candidate, and judges whether the candidate is the same concept, a variant, or genuinely new. No score threshold is applied — every returned neighbor is ranked, none filtered out.
The candidate is embedded server-side using the same symmetric document format as the stored embeddings (`title: <label>: <candidate_name> | text: <candidate_text>`) with `RETRIEVAL_DOCUMENT` task type, so candidate-vs-stored cosine distance is meaningful. When `candidate_text` is omitted, the candidate name alone is used as the embedding text.
Writer-only endpoint (consumes embedding API quota); `concept_type` is restricted to the agent's writable labels (Page, Workflow, Feature). Returns 503 when the embedding service is unavailable, so the caller treats it as a transient failure rather than reading an empty neighborhood as "this candidate is unique".

200.description: Top-K similar nodes (may be empty when no concepts of the given label exist).

post.description: Approves or denies a pending approval. A SELF approval is decided only by the person the agent acts for; a WORKSPACE approval by a workspace owner or editor. Agents and API keys never decide. A support admin decides their own SELF approvals, but never a WORKSPACE approval or anyone else's. An approval may be used only while the policy still asks for it: one the policy now blocks is refused with 409. Once approved, the agent repeats the identical request with the X-Mabl-Approval header naming the approval. An approval is bound to the operation, action, path and query parameters and any body fields the operation binds, such as a merge's from and to; other body content is not bound. The identical request is let through as often as it is repeated until use_expires_time.

parameters.name: workspace_id
parameters.description: The id of the workspace the approval belongs to.

parameters.name: approval_id
parameters.description: The id of the approval.

409.description: The approval is no longer pending (decided, cancelled or expired), or the workspace's guardrails now block the request it asks for.

post.summary: Cancel or revoke a guardrail approval
post.description: Cancels a pending approval, or revokes an approved one, so it can no longer be decided or used. A revoked approval keeps who approved it and when. Allowed to whoever may decide it; agents and API keys are refused.

post.summary: Arm a trigger that wakes an agent
post.description:
Arms a one-shot trigger on this session. An event trigger fires when the named entity reaches the named event; a timer trigger, not yet supported, would fire at a time or on an interval until it expires. Firing queues a message in the session's inbox and starts the agent if nothing is running. A session run locally is refused, and so is watching one, since neither a wake nor its lifecycle events reach it.
A trigger registered for something that has already happened fires immediately, so a caller never has to check first. Sending the same idempotency_key to the same session again returns the trigger stored the first time.

200.description: The trigger stored earlier under the same idempotency_key; nothing new was armed.

429.description: The session, the workspace or the watched entity already holds the most armed triggers allowed; nothing was armed.

delete.description: Disarms a trigger so it never fires. Idempotent: a trigger that already fired, was already disarmed, or does not exist answers the same way.

post.summary: Exchange an API key for an external agent token
post.description: Exchanges a workspace API key, sent with Basic authentication, for a short-lived external_agent access token for a coding agent the key connected. The token acts for the key: it reaches only the key's workspace, with the key's scopes within the external_agent ceiling, and stops working when the key is disabled, expired or deleted. Nothing is stored; exchange again before the token expires. Agent tokens, people's tokens, and login, impersonation, invitation, agent-bound, company and global keys are refused.

401.description: The credential is not valid or is not an exchangeable workspace API key.

post.summary: Record something the user did, for the agent running this session
post.description:
Tells the agent running this session that the user did something in a client — edited the test configuration it saved, pointed the session at a test, a test case or a tracker issue, or attached a file — and does the server-side work that makes it true.
Separate from the inbox because the inbox is a caller speaking. The sender recorded there is derived from the authenticated caller precisely so a caller cannot claim a person typed something, which leaves a client with no way to report a user action except to write prose and send it as the user's own words. These actions are mabl speaking: the caller names an action and its metadata, the server composes the text and queues it as `system`, so what the model reads is versioned with the API rather than assembled in each client.
The server also does the work the action implies, and records none of it on the session. An agent session's artifacts belong to the turn that is running — a turn writes its whole merged set, built from what it loaded, and artifacts merge by name — so anything written into them from outside is replaced by that turn's stale copy. Nothing here writes one.
An attachment's bytes go to the workspace's own storage, under a path derived from the session and the id and recorded nowhere. The agent finds the file by the id this message gives it, so a caller never supplies and never learns a location: one it supplied would be forged by definition, and there is no string that would resolve anywhere else.
A reference is announced and validated, not stored. Reading one back still takes the reference list a planning client maintains; an agent keeping its own note of what it was told is a separate change.

200.description: The queued message, plus the identifier the agent will know the referenced or attached thing by. On a repeat of an idempotency key this is the message stored the first time, and nothing new was queued.

patch.description: Partial update of the resumable subset of an agent session's `startup_params` field, used by the cloud Test Authoring Agent (TAA) continuation flow to roll the session's "latest used / next to be used" authoring context forward. All fields are optional; only fields present in the body are written. Creation-attribution fields on the underlying `startup_params` (`agent_session_source`, `test_variant_id`) and the polymorphic discriminator (`type`) are preserved unchanged across every call — this endpoint is NOT a full partial-update of the `startup_params` JSON object. Only sessions whose `agent_type` is `test_authoring` accept this update; other agent types receive a 409. Uses If-Match for optimistic locking against concurrent updates.

post.summary: Begin resuming an agent session (flip it to the transient `resuming` status)
post.description: Atomically transitions a resumable test-authoring session to the transient `resuming` status, BEFORE the resume planner runs. This is the concurrency guard for the cloud TAA continuation flow: two concurrent answers to the same `needs_attention` session cannot both run a planner or spawn competing cloud instances, because only one wins the flip to `resuming` and the loser gets a 409. Granted only when the session's `latest_instance_status` is resumable (`needs_attention`, `failed`, or `completed`), or it is already `resuming` but stale (last updated longer ago than the server-side TTL — a crashed attempt, safe to steal). A live (non-stale) `resuming` session returns 409. The session leaves `resuming` when the resume spawns a new instance (→ `queued`) or via a `status_update` on the messages endpoint (re-clarification / error restore); a crashed attempt is reclaimed by the next answer's TTL steal. Only `test_authoring` sessions accept this call.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the agent session

200.description: The agent session, now in the `resuming` status

post.summary: Record the outcome of reviewing a finished test-authoring session
post.description: Records what the user decided about a finished `test_authoring` session, flipping it to the reviewed outcome: `accepted` when they kept the authored work, `closed` when they discarded it. A status write only, unless the caller opts into `delete_test` alongside `closed` — see that field. Nothing is ever deleted implicitly, and no branch is deleted at all. Valid for creation and edit sessions alike. Granted only from `completed` or `needs_attention`, enforced inside the write transaction; every other status is a 409, including an already-reviewed session, so a repeated call is rejected rather than silently succeeding. Session-level like `merged` (the cloud instance keeps its own status) and terminal: a reviewed session cannot be resumed, reviewed again, spawned on, or have its status rewritten through updateAgentSession. The conversation is retained either way, so a closed task can be regenerated from it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the agent session

200.description: The agent session, now holding the reviewed outcome

post.summary: Attach artifacts to an agent session
post.description: Attaches artifacts to an agent session without writing a message. Additive: each supplied artifact is merged into the session's `related_artifacts` under the same identity rule the message endpoints use — inline artifacts by `name`, remote artifacts by `entity_kind` + `entity_id` — with the supplied artifact winning on a collision and everything else left untouched. Re-sending the same artifact is therefore idempotent. Returns the session's merged artifact list, not the whole session. Use this, rather than the message endpoints, to record a link (a deployment event, a test run, another agent session) onto a session that is not otherwise being written to.

LinkAccessRoleEnum.description:
A role that may be admitted to a Link (mablnet) tunnel's published services, as named in member_access_roles.

`company_admin` is the company OWNER: of the owning workspace's company for a workspace-owned tunnel, of the company itself for a company-owned one. The three workspace roles mean that role in the owning workspace; on a company-owned tunnel they mean that role in any workspace belonging to the company.

created_by_id.description: created by user id

last_updated_time.description: last updated time, epoch millis

last_updated_by_id.description: last update by user id

enable_link_access_by_support.description: When true, a mabl support admin may reach the tunnel's published services, such as the SOCKS proxy and reachability probes. When false they may still reach the tunnel's control plane — draining a host, inspecting carriers — which is never gated, but no traffic-carrying service.

member_access_roles.description:
Which member roles may reach the tunnel's published services with their own credentials — the tunnel's audience. A caller is admitted when they hold at least one role named here, so holding a role is necessary and never sufficient: the owner has to have named it. An empty array admits nobody, which is where every owner starts, and leaves only api keys — cloud execution is unaffected.

Absent and empty both admit nobody; the difference is about the PATCH, not about access. A PATCH omitting this field leaves the audience as it is, and one sending an empty array clears it.

LinkAccessConfig.description:
Consent settings governing who may reach a Link (mablnet) tunnel owned by this workspace or company. Deliberately separate from support_access_config: not all of this has anything to do with support, and reaching a customer's network is a distinct decision from seeing their workspace.

This is the set an owner of either kind carries. A workspace additionally carries enable_personal_tunnels — see WorkspaceLinkAccessConfig, which extends this. That flag is meaningless for a company: a personal tunnel belongs to a user, and both halves of the decision it governs are asked of a workspace.

Everything here is opt-in. An absent config, and an absent setting within a present config, both admit nobody. The exception is a workspace on a trial account, which reads each setting its owner has not set as the most permissive value — support may reach the tunnel, every role is admitted, personal tunnels are allowed — and is returned that way. Those defaults are never stored, so they end with the trial. None of this affects api-key access to a tunnel — an `execution` key reaching a tunnel for a cloud test run is unaffected throughout.

WorkspaceLinkAccessConfig.description: A workspace's consent flags: everything an owner of either kind carries, plus enable_personal_tunnels, which only a workspace has.

enable_personal_tunnels.description: When true, members of this workspace may start personal tunnels, and this workspace may route cloud test traffic to one. A user may start a personal tunnel if any workspace they belong to allows it, since no single workspace owns it; but only a workspace that allows them may send its runs through one.

member_access_roles.description: Replaces the audience wholesale — send the roles that should be admitted, not a delta, and an empty array to admit nobody. See LinkAccessConfig.member_access_roles

LinkAccessConfigUpdate.description: Consent changes for a workspace or company, applied by PATCH. Every field is optional and only the fields present are applied — omitting one leaves it as it is, which is not the same as sending false or an empty array. The audit fields on LinkAccessConfig are server-owned and so are absent here.

WorkspaceLinkAccessConfigUpdate.description: Consent changes for a workspace, applied by PATCH. Adds the workspace-only flag to the set both owner kinds share.

UsageReportGranularity.description: Time bucket size used for grouping test run results. `daily` aligns buckets to midnight UTC. `weekly` aligns to Monday 00:00 UTC of each ISO-8601 week. `monthly` aligns to the first day of each calendar month at 00:00 UTC.

UsageReportGroupBy.description: Dimension applied to break usage report results down by. `plan` emits one bucket per (time period, plan_id); `application` emits one bucket per (time period, application_id); `workspace` emits one bucket per (time period, workspace_id) and only appears on account-level responses.

start_time.description: Inclusive start of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request.

end_time.description: Exclusive end of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request.

time_buckets.description: Time-bucketed count results. Ordered by `bucket_start_time` ascending, then by `group_id` ascending when `group_by` is set. Buckets with zero matching runs are omitted — if you expect a continuous series, fill gaps on the consumer side using the request `start_time`/`end_time` and `granularity`.

UsageTestRunCountsResponse.description: Response payload for the test run counts endpoint. Contains the resolved query range, the granularity and `group_by` dimension that were applied, and one entry in `time_buckets` per (time period, group_id) combination.

bucket_start_time.description: Inclusive start of the time bucket as Unix epoch milliseconds. Aligned to midnight UTC, Monday 00:00 UTC, or first-of-month 00:00 UTC per the selected granularity.

bucket_end_time.description: Exclusive end of the time bucket as Unix epoch milliseconds. Equal to the `bucket_start_time` of the following period for that bucket size.

group_id.description: ID of the grouping dimension value. Only present when the request specifies `group_by`; omitted otherwise. The value is a plan ID when `group_by=plan`, an application ID when `group_by=application`, or a workspace ID when `group_by=workspace` (account-level endpoints only). Without `group_by` you get one bucket per time period; with `group_by` you get one bucket per (time period x dimension value), so consumers can break down counts or minutes by plan, application, or workspace.

group_name.description: Human-readable name of the group corresponding to `group_id`. Populated on a best-effort basis — may be absent for deleted or otherwise unresolvable entities. Not guaranteed unique; use `group_id` for joins.

total_test_runs.description: Total number of test runs that started within this bucket and match all filters on the request. Includes runs that are still in flight (have started but not yet completed).

passed_test_runs.description: Subset of `total_test_runs` that completed successfully (status is `completed` and `success` is true). In-flight runs are excluded.

failed_test_runs.description: Subset of `total_test_runs` that did not pass — this covers runs that completed with `success: false`, runs that were terminated, and runs that are still in flight (counted as not-yet-passed). `passed_test_runs` plus `failed_test_runs` equals `total_test_runs`.

UsageTestRunCountBucket.description: Aggregated test run counts for a single time bucket, optionally further scoped to a single grouping dimension value when `group_by` is set on the request.

start_time.description: Inclusive start of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request.

end_time.description: Exclusive end of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request.

time_buckets.description: Time-bucketed execution second results. Ordered by `bucket_start_time` ascending, then `group_id` ascending when `group_by` is set. Buckets with zero matching completed runs are omitted.

UsageExecutionSecondsResponse.description: Response payload for the execution seconds endpoint. Contains the resolved query range, granularity, and `group_by` dimension, plus one `time_buckets` entry per (time period, group_id) combination with at least one completed run.

bucket_start_time.description: Inclusive start of the time bucket as Unix epoch milliseconds. Aligned to midnight UTC, Monday 00:00 UTC, or first-of-month 00:00 UTC per the selected granularity.

bucket_end_time.description: Exclusive end of the time bucket as Unix epoch milliseconds. Equal to the `bucket_start_time` of the following period for that bucket size.

group_id.description: ID of the grouping dimension value. Only present when the request specifies `group_by`; omitted otherwise. The value is a plan ID when `group_by=plan`, an application ID when `group_by=application`, or a workspace ID when `group_by=workspace` (account-level endpoints only). Without `group_by` you get one bucket per time period; with `group_by` you get one bucket per (time period x dimension value), so consumers can break down counts or minutes by plan, application, or workspace.

group_name.description: Human-readable name of the group corresponding to `group_id`. Populated on a best-effort basis — may be absent for deleted or otherwise unresolvable entities. Not guaranteed unique; use `group_id` for joins.

total_execution_seconds.description: Sum of (end_time - start_time) in whole seconds across every completed run whose `start_time` falls within the bucket. Measures time spent executing, not time queued. In-flight runs are excluded.

total_test_runs.description: Number of completed runs contributing to `total_execution_seconds`. Excludes in-flight runs. This is NOT the same as the equivalent field on `testRunCounts`, which includes in-flight runs.

UsageExecutionSecondsBucket.description: Aggregated execution time for a single time bucket, optionally scoped to a grouping dimension value when `group_by` is set. Only completed runs are included in this bucket's totals.

bucket_start_time.description: Inclusive start of the day (midnight UTC) as Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum test run concurrency is always computed against UTC calendar days.

bucket_end_time.description: Exclusive end of the day (midnight UTC of the next day) as Unix epoch milliseconds. Always 24 hours after `bucket_start_time`.

max_test_run_concurrency.description: Maximum number of test runs of the queried `test_type` that were executing simultaneously at any instant during this day. Computed via a sweep-line over run start/end times in the underlying billable events data.

UsageMaxTestRunConcurrencyBucket.description: Maximum concurrent test runs observed during a single UTC calendar day. One bucket is emitted per day in the queried range that had at least one matching run.

workspace_id.description: Identifier of the workspace this block describes. Always populated with this block's workspace identifier.

start_time.description: Inclusive start of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request (or the default-derived value when the request omits it).

end_time.description: Exclusive end of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request (or the default-derived value when the request omits it).

configured_test_run_concurrency_limit.description: The workspace's configured maximum concurrent test runs for the requested `test_type` at the time of the query. For `browser`, this is the sum of the workspace's Linux, macOS, and Windows browser quotas. For `api`, `mobile`, or `performance`, this is the single numeric quota for that resource. Returns `0` if the workspace has no configured quota for the requested test type. Compare `max_test_run_concurrency` against this value to see how close the workspace is running to its purchased capacity.

time_buckets.description: Daily-only time buckets for this endpoint. One entry per UTC calendar day in the queried range that had any runs of the requested test type. Ordered by `bucket_start_time` ascending. Days with no runs are omitted.

WorkspaceMaxTestRunConcurrencyResponse.description: Daily maximum concurrent test run data for a single workspace, along with the workspace's configured test run concurrency limit for comparison. On the workspace endpoint this is the top-level response object. On the account endpoint it appears once per workspace within the `workspaces` array.

start_time.description: Inclusive start of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request (or the default-derived value when the request omits it).

end_time.description: Exclusive end of the queried time range as Unix epoch milliseconds, echoed from the request (or the default-derived value when the request omits it).

workspaces.description: One entry per workspace in the account the caller has access to (or the single entry corresponding to the `workspace_id` query parameter when that is set). Each entry is a full `WorkspaceMaxTestRunConcurrencyResponse` including its own daily maximum test run concurrency buckets and configured limit.

AccountMaxTestRunConcurrencyResponse.description: Daily maximum concurrent test run data for every workspace the caller has access to within an account. Each workspace carries its own `configured_test_run_concurrency_limit`, which may differ across workspaces in the same account.

Saved through test_objective: a full save may set it alongside steps as one version, and omitting it keeps the stored one. TestObjectiveCheck.description:
One verdict on whether the steps of a test version satisfy that version's objective summary. Stored apart from the test, so recording one never creates a test version, and never carried to a new version.
Scoped to the step list stored on that version. Steps reached through a referenced flow are not covered: a flow is held by ID and resolved to a version at run time, and that resolution depends on the branch, so editing a referenced flow, or reading the test from a branch that resolves it differently, can leave the check describing steps it never saw.

test_id.description: The test invariant ID

gap.description: How the steps fall short of the summary. Required for accepted_gap, optional for drifted, and dropped for aligned.

TestObjectiveCheckRequest.description: A verdict on whether a test version's steps satisfy its objective summary.

TestObjectiveCheckState.description: aligned means the steps satisfy the summary; drifted means they fall short, with the difference in gap; accepted_gap means a person saw that gap and chose to keep it.

TestObjectiveState.description:
Whether the steps of this test version have been checked against the objective summary, and what the check found. unverified means the summary has not been checked against these steps; aligned means it was checked and the steps satisfy it; drifted means it was checked and the steps fall short, with the difference in gap; accepted_gap means the user saw that gap and chose to keep it.
Scoped to the step list stored on this version. Steps reached through a referenced flow are not covered: a flow is held by ID and resolved to a version at run time, and that resolution depends on the branch, so editing a referenced flow, or reading this version from a branch that resolves it differently, can leave the state describing steps the check never saw.

FlowRole.description: The role this flow plays in the test. A teardown flow always runs at the end of the test, even if an earlier flow failed. Teardown flows must form a contiguous block at the end of the test's flow list. Defaults to normal.

iteration_value.description: A number, the name of the variable containing the number, a range of values to iterate over, a CSS query whose matching elements are iterated over (one iteration per matched element when iteration_type is elements), or the name of a variable whose array value is iterated over (one iteration per array element when iteration_type is variable_array; a non-array value iterates once). Not used when iteration_type is condition, which carries its condition in iteration_condition instead.

iteration_condition.description: Required when iteration_type is condition. A single step in the json_steps format, keyed If, in the same shape a conditional step group uses - for example {"If": {"target": {...}, "condition": {...}, "actionCode": "conditional_if"}}. It is evaluated before each iteration and the loop runs for as long as it holds, so a condition that is false to begin with runs the flow zero times. See iteration_limit for what happens when the loop hits its cap.

iteration_count_variable.description: Optional variable name (elements iteration only). When set, the number of elements the loop iterated over is written to a variable with this name once the loop completes, so later steps can reference it.

iteration_limit.description: Optional maximum number of iterations (elements, variable_array, and condition iteration only). When set, the loop runs at most this many iterations even if more elements match or the array is longer. Capped at the system maximum of 500. Elements and variable_array loops stop quietly on reaching it; a condition loop whose condition still holds at the cap fails the step.

prefetch.description: Optional (elements iteration only). When true, the loop counts all matching elements once at the start and iterates by index, which is navigation-safe; use it when the loop body navigates away from or reloads the page (for example clicking each matching row to open a detail page and then returning). When false or unset, the loop marks the matched DOM elements and revisits them each iteration, which is faster but breaks if the page changes between iterations.
