MablnetInfrastructureKeysResponse.description: The link infrastructure keys in use across the deployment.

key.description: The cluster key (`mabl` = the shared multi-tenant cluster).

wss_fqdn.description: Derived WSS carrier hostname (`<key>-wss.<domain>`). Absent when the deployment has no mablnet domain configured.

quic_fqdn.description: Derived QUIC carrier hostname (`<key>-quic.<domain>:443`). Absent when the deployment has no mablnet domain configured.

company_ids.description: Companies holding this key (empty for `mabl` — shared-cluster residency is the keyless default, not an assignment).

MablnetInfrastructureKey.description: One link infrastructure cluster key and the companies pinned to it.

operator_public_key.description: Base64-encoded X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the deployment's operator-token Ed25519 public key. A Host registers the `mablnet-operator` command service (and verifies per-command operator tokens) against this key. Absent when the deployment has no operator-token signing key configured — in that case the Host runs without the operator interface.

signed_bundle.description:
The publisher-signed trust envelope, forwarded byte-for-byte as it was published. An Agent verifies these exact bytes against the publisher key embedded in its own binary and takes its trust anchors from inside the envelope, which is what makes the anchors safe to fetch over a channel the Agent cannot authenticate — most customers run TLS-intercepting proxies, so the Agent does not verify this connection's certificate.
Carried as an opaque string rather than as fields on this schema on purpose: the signature covers the bytes the publisher produced, and spreading them across this schema would mean reserialising them through a generated model that silently drops any field it does not yet know about. Do not parse, reformat, or re-emit it — pass it through.
Always present when this endpoint returns 200. An unsigned trust bundle is refused rather than served, because anchors an Agent cannot verify are the problem the signature exists to solve; the endpoint reports the deployment as unconfigured until the bundle has been published signed.

MablnetPeerCa.description:
Mablnet deployment trust material. The trust anchors live *inside* `signed_bundle`, not beside it: a client verifies that envelope against the publisher key embedded in its own binary and takes the anchors from within.
This response therefore carries no plain rendering of those anchors. It used to, and every consumer ignored it — anchors handed over unsigned are exactly the ones nothing can verify, so serving them only offered a caller a way to get the trust decision wrong.
The optional `operator_public_key` carries the deployment's operator-token Ed25519 public key, so a Host can verify operator-command tokens (and admit the operator interface) without a separate fetch. It rides this response because it is the same kind of artifact — a deployment-wide, non-secret mablnet trust root — and folds into this response's ETag, so a key rotation invalidates the conditional-GET cache.

owner_id.description: The resolved owner id — the run's workspace id for a workspace tunnel, the company id for a company tunnel. This is the SOCKS5 username a client presents to the agent's socks5 service, whose tripwire is `(owner_id, label)`.

label.description: The resolved tunnel's Link label — the second half of the SOCKS5 tripwire `(owner_id, label)`. Echoed so a caller resolving several tunnels at once (e.g. all of a user's live personal tunnels) can tell them apart.

carrier_endpoints.description: The deployment's mablnet Router FQDN for each available carrier protocol, keyed by the `LinkAgentProtocolEnum` value (`mablnet_wss`, `mablnet_quic`). Bare hosts; the client normalises each to its scheme (`wss://` / `udp://`). A protocol absent from the map isn't offered by this deployment (e.g. QUIC before it has rolled out to the region).

allowed_protocols.description: The set of mablnet carrier protocols this tunnel is allowed to use — the mabl-controlled policy, operator-tunable per tunnel via `LinkLabel.operator_tunables_overrides`. Order is not significant. Only `mablnet_*` values appear, and every entry has a matching key in `carrier_endpoints`. The client picks the best available protocol from this set, and the fallback order among them, using local signals the operator can't know (UDP-buffer clamp, proxy in the path, reachability).

carrier_connect_timeouts.description: Per-protocol carrier establishment deadline in milliseconds, keyed by `LinkAgentProtocolEnum` value — how long the client waits for a carrier on that protocol to JOIN before falling back to the next protocol it tries (from `allowed_protocols`). The mabl-controlled, operator-tunable default (`{mablnet_quic: 8000, mablnet_wss: 45000}`); a protocol absent from the map uses the client's built-in default.

client_pool_size.description: Multi-carrier peer-pool size the client leg should boot for this tunnel, present only when the operator pinned one (the tunable `mablnet_client_pool_size`). Absent means the client auto-selects a fixed pool size from its own machine's resources (total memory, capped by cores). An explicit N > 1 boots N mablnet Hosts — one slot identity each, each with its own carriers — and spreads connections across them, lifting the one-pinned-carrier-per-peer throughput cap for many-connection workloads; `1` = pool off. Treat explicit values < 1 as 1.

has_live_agent.description: True when a `ready` Link Agent advertising a mablnet carrier for the resolved owner + label has heartbeated within the liveness window. The executor's pre-run serviceability gate.

mablnet_tenant_id_hex.description: Zero-padded 8-character lowercase hex of the tunnel's mablnet tenant id, when the resolved Link Label carries one. Diagnostic / correlation aid; not required to connect.

infrastructure_key.description: The link infrastructure cluster key the `carrier_endpoints` belong to — the owning company's resolved key for workspace/company tunnels, the announce-time placement recorded on the Link Label for personal tunnels. Lets consumers apply cluster-eligibility rules (e.g. the personal-tunnel stripe-set filter) without re-resolving.

MablnetTunnelTarget.description: The resolved mablnet tunnel a cloud test run should reach for a `(workspace_id, label)`, returned by `GET /link/mablnet/tunnels/resolve`. Unlike the legacy path's list of Link Servers, a mablnet tunnel is a single tenant reached by dialing a mablnet Router; intra-tenant load-balancing across the tunnel's agents is the Router's job, so one target (not a list) is returned per label. The client connects with a carrier from `carrier_endpoints`, choosing the best of the `allowed_protocols` (and the fallback order among them) from what it knows locally.

owner_id.description: The workspace id or company id (per `owner_type`) the session operates on.

label.description: Tunnel (Link Label) within the owner the operator session targets.

MablnetOperatorSessionRequest.description: Request body for `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/operator/tenant`. Specifies which tunnel the operator session targets. Both minted artifacts (peer credential + operator token) bind to this `(owner_type, owner_id, label)` tunnel, which maps to one mablnet tenant.

label.description: Optional audit / host-id readability label for the session (e.g. an incident id). Defaults server-side when omitted. Does not bind the session to any customer tunnel.

infrastructure_key.description: The link infrastructure key of the cluster whose fleet this session operates (`mabl` when omitted — the shared cluster). The minted operator token carries it as its `infrastructure_key` claim, and a Router only accepts fleet tokens naming its own cluster — so operating a dedicated customer's fleet requires minting against that cluster's key.

MablnetFleetOperatorSessionRequest.description: Request body for `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/operator/fleet`. A fleet operator session operates on the Link Router fleet itself, not a customer tunnel, so it takes no `workspace_id` — both minted artifacts bind to the fleet sentinel workspace. The only field is an optional audit label; the api defaults it when absent.

peer_credential.description: Base64 (standard alphabet, no URL safety) of the UTF-8 JSON bytes of the signed peer JOIN credential. The caller presents these bytes as the mablnet `HostCredentials` blob at JOIN; api's `/authorize/host` validates the Ed25519 signature and admits the user as a tenant peer.

operator_token.description: Base64 (standard alphabet, no URL safety) of the UTF-8 JSON bytes of the signed operator-command token. Carried per-request in `OperatorCommand.token` and validated by the customer Host's `MablOperatorAuthorizer`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp marking when both artifacts expire. Fixed 30-minute window from issue time.

MablnetOperatorSessionResponse.description: Result of a successful `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/operator/tenant` or `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/operator/fleet` call. Carries both artifacts the caller needs for one operator session: a peer JOIN credential and an operator-command token.

owner_id.description: The workspace id or company id (per `owner_type`) the user is joining.

workspace_id.description: Deprecated alias for a workspace owner (`owner_type=workspace`, `owner_id=<workspace_id>`). Prefer `owner_type` + `owner_id`.

label.description: Tunnel (Link Label) within the owner the user is joining.

host_id.description: Optional. When present the minted credential reuses this `host_id` rather than generating a fresh one, so a long-lived peer session can refresh its credential without changing the Host identity the Router has bound. Shape-only for the peer path — the credential's Ed25519 signature still binds it to the authorized (user, owner, label).

MablnetPeerCredentialRequest.description: Request body for `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/peer`. Specifies which customer tunnel the user wants to JOIN as a peer: an owner (`owner_type` + `owner_id`, a workspace or a company) plus the `label`. `workspace_id` is a deprecated alias for `owner_type=workspace` + `owner_id=<workspace_id>`, accepted for older callers — supply either the owner pair or `workspace_id`.

peer_credential.description: Base64 (standard alphabet, no URL safety) of the UTF-8 JSON bytes of the signed peer JOIN credential. Same shape as the `peer_credential` returned from `/authorize/operator/tenant`.

expires_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp marking when the credential expires. Fixed 30-minute window from issue time.

MablnetPeerCredentialResponse.description: Result of a successful `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/peer` call. Carries one signed peer JOIN credential bound to the requested workspace.

manifest.description: Base64 of the exact signed manifest bytes. Decode, then verify + parse per manifest-format.md.

resolved_channel.description: The channel the returned manifest was resolved on, after channel aliasing and any per-tenant release override. Equals the requested channel unless one of those redirected it. A consumer that checks the manifest's signed channel compares it to this, so a renamed channel keeps working; the check catches a manifest moved between channels by a publishing mistake or a middlebox, not a substitution by the api itself, which the signature covers.

rollout_schedule.description: Optional rollout schedule for this publish. Omit for the default gradual staged schedule (prod / `stable`). Pass a single `[{percent: 100, since_ms: 0}]` stage to make the version current fleet-wide immediately — used for the `dev`/latest and per-branch channels, where the (typically single) tracking Host must resolve to the new build at once rather than wait out the gradual ramp. api-only orchestration metadata; rides outside the signed manifest bytes, so it does not affect the manifest's signature.

MablnetManifestEnvelope.description: Transport envelope carrying a signed mablnet worker release manifest as opaque bytes. The `manifest` field is the **exact** signed manifest document (structure: `manifest-format.md in link/mablnet/docs` § Schema), base64-encoded so it survives the api's JSON layer byte-for-byte — the api never deserialises or reformats the manifest, which is what keeps its Ed25519/JCS signature verifiable on the consumer. The mabl-API transport wraps the manifest this way; the GCS and update-service transports return the same bytes unwrapped, so an API-channel consumer decodes this field before verifying.

keystore.description: Base64 of the exact signed keystore bytes. Decode, then verify + parse per manifest-format.md.

MablnetKeystoreEnvelope.description: Transport envelope carrying a signed mablnet publisher keystore as opaque bytes (structure: `manifest-format.md` § Keystore document format). Same rationale as `MablnetManifestEnvelope` — base64 of the exact signed bytes so the signature survives the api's JSON layer untouched.

id.description: Datastore key for this entity — `<artifact>/<channel>` (one entity per artifact + channel). Server-set.

channel.description: Release channel this state governs, within `artifact`.

current_version.description: The version being rolled out to (Hosts inside the rolled-out percentage receive this).

fallback_version.description: What Hosts not yet inside the rollout receive. Unset once a rollout reaches 100% and the current version is fully rolled out.

rollout_schedule.description: Time-based stages; the rolled-out percentage is the max stage whose `since_ms` has elapsed since `published_at`.

force_percent.description: When set, overrides the time-based schedule with an explicit rolled-out percentage (operator force-advance). Cleared by resuming the schedule.

published_at.description: When the current rollout started; the schedule's `since_ms` offsets are relative to this.

paused.description: When true, the manifest endpoint stops advancing the rollout — Hosts stay on whichever version they have.

MablnetRolloutState.description: Per-channel staged-rollout state owned by the api (one entity per artifact + channel). Unlike the manifest/keystore this is api-owned data, not a signed document, so normal date-time handling applies. The manifest endpoint reads this to decide which version a given Host receives — see design doc § Manifest resolution.

percent.description: Target rolled-out percentage at this stage (0–100).

since_ms.description: Milliseconds after `published_at` at which this stage becomes active.

MablnetRolloutStage.description: One stage of a staged rollout — `percent` of Hosts get the current version once `since_ms` has elapsed.

paused.description: Pause (true) or resume (false) the staged rollout.

force_percent.description: Force the rolled-out percentage to this explicit value (0–100), overriding the schedule.

MablnetRolloutUpdate.description: Body for `PATCH /link/mablnet/artifacts/{artifact}/releases/{version}/rollout`. All fields optional; supply the one(s) you want to change. `paused` toggles pause/resume; `force_percent` overrides the time-based schedule with an explicit percentage.

version.description: The already-stored release version to make current on this channel.

rollout_schedule.description: Optional rollout schedule override for the forced version; defaults to the standard staged schedule.

MablnetChannelCurrent.description: Body for `PUT /link/mablnet/artifacts/{artifact}/channels/{channel}/current`. Forces the channel's current to an already-stored version (rollback / pin). Optionally overrides the rollout schedule for the forced version (e.g. a single 100%/0ms stage for an immediate fleet-wide swap).

id.description: Datastore key for this entity — `<artifact>/<alias channel>`. Server-set.

artifact.description: Release artifact the alias and its target belong to. Server-set.

target.description: The channel (within the same artifact) the alias resolves to. May itself be an alias (chains are followed), but must not equal the alias name and must not form a cycle.

MablnetChannelAlias.description: Declares one release channel to be an alias of another. When set, the api resolves every request for the alias channel (manifest resolution + the operator rollout ops) to the `target` channel's state, so a client that still sends the old name keeps working after a rename. Aliases are scoped to one artifact: the artifact and alias name are the `{artifact}` / `{channel}` path segments; the body carries only `target`. See design doc `release-channel-aliasing-and-selection.md in link/mablnet/docs`.

MablnetReleaseChannel.description: The well-known mablnet worker release channels. `latest` is the newest auto-published main build (immediate 100%) — the dev / non-prod track; `stable` is the tag-promoted release with a gradual rollout ramp — the prod track. The channel wire value is free-form (ephemeral per-branch channels exist and are passed via override), so endpoints accept any string; this enum names the two canonical channels a client should select between by environment (dev → `latest`, prod → `stable`) instead of hardcoding a literal. See design doc `release-channel-aliasing-and-selection.md in link/mablnet/docs`.

channel.description: Channel this tenant follows instead of the one its Host requests (e.g. `latest`, `stable`, or a branch name as published). Unset = use the requested channel. The effective channel is alias-resolved, so a channel alias applies here too.

version.description: Exact worker version pinned for this tenant, bypassing the staged rollout. Unset = follow the (effective) channel's rollout.

MablnetWorkerReleaseOverride.description: Per-tenant override of the worker release a Link Label receives, set by a mabl operator (not customer-writable). Consulted by `GET /link/mablnet/artifacts/mablnet-host/manifest` before the channel's staged rollout: `channel` (when set) replaces the channel the Host requested; `version` (when set) pins that exact version, bypassing the staged percentage. Either or both may be set; an absent override means the tenant follows the normal channel rollout. Used to give one customer an experimental or branch build to confirm a fix, then cleared once the version is promoted channel-wide via `PUT /link/mablnet/artifacts/mablnet-host/channels/{channel}/current`.

created_time.description: Time at which the Link Label was created

label.description: The link label

cloud_safe_canonical_name.description: The globally unique name for this label that is safe to use in FQDNs (based on label and workspace ID).

client_certificate.description: The serialized X.509 certificate Link Agents use as their client identity on the legacy Link Tunnel mTLS path. Not used by mablnet: mablnet's `HostCredentials` are a separate JSON blob (workspace_id + label + host_id + issued_at + nonce); the mabl-deployment `HostAuthenticator` validates that blob via the `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/host` endpoint and maps it to `mablnet_tenant_id`. Also distinct from the per-Host peer QUIC certs mablnet's `CertificateAuthority` issues at join time, which embed `(tenantId, hostId)` in SAN OtherName extensions.

server_certificate.description: The serialized certificate for Link Servers to use

client_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the client certificate

client_public_key.description: The public key of the client certificate

server_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the server certificate

server_public_key.description: The public key of the server certificate

link_server_image_tag.description: If specified, overrides the default Link Server image tag in this environment

termination_time.description: The time this was terminated at

terminated_by_id.description: The client id that terminated this link labe;l

workspace_id.description: The workspace that owns this label, for `workspace`-owned tunnels. Also the identity the legacy Link Tunnel path and the per-label mTLS certs are keyed by. Unset for `company`-owned tunnels (which are mablnet-only) — read `owner_type`/`owner_id` for the canonical scope.

owner_id.description: The id of the owning entity — equals `workspace_id` for `workspace` tunnels, the company id for `company` tunnels.

link_infrastructure_key.description: The link infrastructure cluster this tunnel lives on, recorded for personal (`user`-owned) tunnels only. Server-derived at announce from the owner's workspace associations and folded into the label's identity (the label is a hash of `machine_identity` and this key), so a placement change produces a new tunnel rather than mutating this one. Absent on workspace- and company-owned labels — their placement always derives live from the owning company's `link_infrastructure_key` — and on personal labels announced before placement existed, which live on the shared cluster.

mablnet_tenant_id.description:
32-bit mablnet tenant identifier assigned at LinkLabel creation. Derived deterministically from a stable hash of `<owner-key>:<label>` — where `<owner-key>` is the workspace id for `workspace` tunnels and `company:<company-id>` for `company` tunnels — truncated into the 32-bit unsigned range, with a defensive collision check against existing LinkLabels — on the unlikely event the hash collides with an already-allocated tenant id, the value is offset (by 1 or a small random delta) until it lands in an unused slot. The chosen value is immutable for the lifetime of the LinkLabel. Used as the `tenantId` in mablnet's protocol. Populated lazily for legacy labels during the migration cutover; absent until the LinkLabel has been migrated or recreated.
The legacy mablnet documentation calls this the "tenant id"; mabl's customer-facing name for the same concept is "Link label", and this field ties the two together.

mablnet_tenant_id_hex.description: Zero-padded 8-character lowercase hex form of `mablnet_tenant_id`, e.g. `bee85e2b`. Provided for log/grep/observability ergonomics; the numeric and hex forms always agree (both written in the same pass).

LinkLabel.description: Represents a label used by a Link Agent and Server

LinkLabelQueryResult.description: Represents a list of Link label names

LinkTunnelOwnerType.description: The kind of entity a mablnet tunnel is scoped to — its "owner". `workspace` is the classic scope: one tunnel per workspace. `company` scopes a single tunnel to an entire company, so every workspace under that company shares one mablnet tenant (and one Link Agent fleet) instead of needing a tunnel each. `user` is a personal tunnel scoped to a single user, private to that user — its egress is the user's own machine, used to route a cloud test run through it. All three are mablnet-only: legacy Link Tunnel is always workspace-scoped.

peer_credential.description: Base64 of the verbatim Ed25519-signed peer JOIN credential blob (`{role: "peer", sub, workspace_id, label, host_id, issued_at, expires_at, nonce, signature}` as minted). Present only on the peer path; its presence selects that path.

owner_id.description: The id of the owning entity — a workspace id when `owner_type` is `workspace`, a company id when `company`. Cross-checked against the auth principal: an api-key caller must be scoped to this workspace (or to a company that owns it, or — for a company owner — to a workspace within that company); a user-OAuth caller must be able to modify it. Required on the api-key path.

label.description: The Link Label name within the owner (the customer-facing "tunnel name"). `(owner_type, owner_id, label)` uniquely identifies a tunnel; multiple Hosts can be in the same tunnel concurrently. Required on the api-key path.

host_id.description: Per-Host-instance identifier the caller advertises. For `link_agent` keys this is composite — `<link-agent-id>:<host-bundle-version>` — and the `LinkAgent.id` prefix (the segment before the first `:`, or the whole value when there is none) MUST match an active `LinkAgent.id` in `(workspace_id, label)`; the version suffix is accepted and echoed so each host-bundle generation is a distinct Host. For `execution` keys and user OAuth callers this is validated for shape only (UUID-like or `la-`-prefixed mabl uid, ≤128 chars). Echoed back as `host_identity` in the response.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when the caller constructed this blob. Rejected if more than ±5 minutes from server time (sliding-window replay bound).

nonce.description: 16 random bytes from `SecureRandom`, hex-encoded (32 chars). One-shot uniqueness guard; the server-side cache rejects repeats within a 10 minute window per auth principal.

router_infrastructure_key.description: The link infrastructure key of the Router forwarding this JOIN (its LINK_ROUTER_INFRA_KEY — `mabl` for the shared cluster, the customer key for a dedicated cluster). When present, the api enforces cluster exclusivity for BOTH credential paths: the caller-tenant's resolved key must equal this value or the JOIN is denied (a dedicated company's tunnels cannot ride the shared cluster, and nobody outside the company can join its dedicated cluster). Absent on Routers that predate key-reporting — the check is skipped, which is correct only while such Routers exist; see dedicated-link-infra.md in link/mablnet/docs.

LinkLabelAuthorizationRequest.description:
Authorization request Link Router forwards to this endpoint for a mablnet carrier-join. Spec and rationale: `mablnet-client-authorization.md in link/mablnet/docs`.
Two credential types share this schema, discriminated by the presence of `peer_credential`:
1. `peer_credential` absent — the legacy api-key path. `api_key` flows in the `Authorization: Basic` header; the body carries `owner_type`, `owner_id`, `label`, `host_id`, `issued_at`, `nonce` (all required for this path). Validated against the owner's API keys.
2. `peer_credential` present — an Ed25519-signed credential minted by `/link/mablnet/authorize/operator/tenant` or `/link/mablnet/authorize/peer`, forwarded verbatim as base64 of the exact `HostCredentials` bytes the peer presented at JOIN. The signature is verified over the blob's own canonical body — never over fields reconstructed from this request — and every peer attribute (workspace, label, host id, expiry) is read from the verified blob; the other properties in this schema are ignored for this path. (Fleet operator peer credentials are verified Router-side, not here — they never reach this endpoint.) See `mablnet-client-authorization.md in link/mablnet/docs` § Operator credentials.

tenant_id.description: Unsigned 32-bit mablnet tenant identifier for this tunnel (`[0x00000001, 0xFEFFFFFF]`; system-tenant range `0xFFxxxxxx` reserved). Derived from the LinkLabel; see `mablnet-tenant-id-derivation.md in link/mablnet/docs`.

host_identity.description: The `host_id` the caller supplied, echoed back after caller-type-branched validation. Used by the mablnet library for reconnect-grace bookkeeping.

valid_until.description: RFC 3339 timestamp marking when this authorization expires. Fixed 1h window (`now + 1h`) regardless of caller type. The caller refreshes before this point via another `POST /link/mablnet/authorize/host`.

access.description:
How much of the tenant this peer may reach once admitted. `full` — every service, subject to the usual tenant and visibility rules. `control_plane` — only services the Host registered as control-plane (the operator RPC surface); a stream to anything the Host advertises on its owner's behalf, such as SOCKS or probes, is refused by the Host at accept.
Read off the peer credential's signed `access` claim, so the decision is the one made at mint time. Always present on this response — unlike the credential claim itself, which is omitted when `full` to keep ordinary credentials byte-identical. **An absent value still means `full`**: it is what an api predating this field returns, and what every api-key join carries. Restriction is opted into, never inferred from absence.
The Router records this with the Host's registration and serves it to other Hosts asking `PeerAccessQuery`; see `support-admin-tunnel-access.md in link/mablnet/docs`.

LinkLabelAuthorizationResponse.description: Authorization decision returned to Link Router on a successful call. Maps directly to the mablnet protocol's `AuthenticatedHost` value.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID

use_link_agent.description: Environments only - whether test traffic routes through Link

link_agent_labels.description: Environment labels, or the database connection's default connection property labels. Absent when none are stored.

connection_overrides.description: Database connections only - the labels of every per-environment override

version.description: The entity version, to send as If-Match when updating these labels

LinkLabelUsage.description: The Link label settings of one environment or database connection

environment_id.description: Environment ID of the override

link_agent_labels.description: Labels of the override's connection properties. Absent when none are stored, in which case the override routes by the environment's labels. Required when updating.

LinkLabelUsageOverride.description: The Link labels of a database connection's override for one environment

cursor.description: Cursor for the next page; absent on the last page

link_agent_labels.description: The environment's new labels, replacing the current ones
New labels for the default connection properties; unchanged when omitted

connection_overrides.description: New labels for existing overrides, matched by environment_id; overrides not listed are unchanged

LinkAgentDistributionFormatEnum.description: Archive formats the Link Agent is distributed in, plus `msi` — the Windows installer, which registers the agent as a service so that it starts on boot. `auto_update` does not apply to `msi`: there is a single installer, and a service takes upgrades through the installer rather than through the in-place updater, so the parameter is ignored for that format.

LinkAgentDistributionEnum.description: Which Link Agent distribution an instance is — the Java Link Agent (`java`), the mabl-cli Link Agent (`mabl_cli`), or the personal Link Agent built into the mabl desktop app (`mabl_desktop`).

LinkAgentCapabilityEnum.description:
Optional behaviors a Link Agent has been built to support. Reported by the Agent on startup; mabl-side endpoints gate operator actions on the presence of the relevant capability so that hitting a feature-dependent endpoint against an older Agent (which would silently fail to act on it) is rejected with a clear error.
- `maintenance`: the Agent polls `GET /link/agents/{id}` to learn about
  operator-set state and drains its tunnels when placed into maintenance
  (`status=draining`), reporting `status=drained` once it has finished.

LinkAgentProtocolEnum.description:
Protocol the Link Agent uses to reach the mabl side.
Legacy values (pre-mablnet): - `wss`: WebSocket over TLS to a Link Server (the only one of the three that
  shipped — `ssl` and `https` are historical placeholders).
- `ssl`, `https`: never implemented; kept in the enum for backwards
  compatibility with serialized records that captured them.

New values (mablnet): - `mablnet_wss`: WSS carrier to a mablnet Router, through the Application LB on
  :443. The fallback substrate, and the only one that traverses an HTTP proxy.
- `mablnet_quic`: UDP/QUIC carrier to a mablnet Router, on :443. The preferred
  substrate where the network passes UDP; Agents fall back to `mablnet_wss`
  where it does not.

LinkAgentEndpoint.description: api-set connection target for one protocol's Link Agent → mabl-side connection. Address format is protocol-specific: legacy `wss` carries an `<fqdn>` string (matches the legacy `current_link_server_endpoint` shape); `mablnet_wss` / `mablnet_quic` carry an FQDN that the Agent resolves at connect time. The api is the source of truth for these values — the Agent reads from `endpoints` to learn where to connect and never writes back to it (corresponding agent-set per-protocol health lives in `connection_status`).

is_connected.description: Whether the Agent currently has a working connection on this protocol. Updated on each heartbeat. Per-protocol state lets mabl ops identify accounts where one protocol is failing (e.g. firewall blocking mablnet's :443 while legacy `wss` works) without losing the working path.

last_error.description: Most recent connection error for this protocol, if `is_connected` is false. Empty when the connection is up.

last_connected_time.description: Time of the most recent successful connection on this protocol. Helps operators distinguish "never worked" from "worked recently and just dropped". Absent if the Agent has never seen a successful connection for this protocol.

unreachable_seconds.description:
How long this protocol has been without a working connection, measured by the Agent from its own clock and reset the moment it connects. Absent while `is_connected` is true, and absent on Agents that predate the field.

A duration rather than a timestamp on purpose: the api compares it against a threshold, and a customer host's clock can be arbitrarily skewed from mabl's. This is what lets the api tell a sustained loss of access apart from an Agent that is still on its first connect attempt — see the `link_endpoint_unreachable` advisory.

LinkAgentConnectionStatus.description: Agent-set per-protocol connection health. Keys align with `endpoints` so operators can pair "where the api told the Agent to go" with "what the Agent reports about it". Reported on heartbeat.

drain_started.description: When the Agent was placed into maintenance and began draining (epoch millis).

drain_completed.description: When the Agent finished draining — either all in-flight connections completed or `drain_timeout_seconds` elapsed (status `drained`). Set server-side when the Agent first reports it has drained; absent while the status is still `draining`. When present, the Agent is safe to terminate.

drain_timeout_seconds.description: Operator-supplied upper bound on how long the Agent will wait for in-flight connections to drain before transitioning to `drained`. Omitted for an unbounded wait.

LinkAgentMaintenance.description: Operator-requested maintenance state for a Link Agent. While the Agent's status is `draining` or `drained`, mabl-side routing treats it as ineligible for new traffic (mablnet drains its carriers), but in-flight connections continue to be serviced until they finish or the drain timeout expires. The object persists as a record of the most-recent maintenance window after the Agent returns to service.

drain_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum seconds the Agent should wait for in-flight connections to drain before signalling that it is safe to terminate. Omit to wait indefinitely.

LinkAgentMaintenanceRequest.description: Optional parameters for placing a Link Agent into maintenance mode.

mablnet_min_carriers.description: Steady-state target carrier count for the mablnet Host. PATCH `null` to clear an override and fall back to the next merge layer.

mablnet_max_carriers.description: Advisory ceiling — overlap budget for in-flight carrier churn.

mablnet_join_timeout.description: Per-carrier-join timeout. Tighten only when investigating a misbehaving LB.

mablnet_telemetry_export_interval.description: Cadence at which the Agent-side SDK MeterProvider flushes to the mablnet-metrics-collector. Drop to ~`PT5S` during incidents.

mablnet_carrier_recycle_interval.description: Period between proactive carrier-recycle ticks: the worker retires its oldest carrier (make-before-break, so existing QUIC sessions migrate without disruption) and the LB redistributes the replacement across the Router fleet. Default `PT60M`. Set `PT0S` to disable proactive recycle (the worker still retires unhealthy carriers). PATCH `null` to clear an override.

mablnet_carrier_recycle_jitter.description: Random offset added to the first carrier-recycle tick, to desync the fleet so recycles don't bunch into a thundering-herd reconnect. Default `PT30M`. No effect when `mablnet_carrier_recycle_interval` is `PT0S`.

mablnet_allowed_protocols.description: The set of mablnet carrier protocols this tunnel is allowed to use (default `[mablnet_quic, mablnet_wss]`). This is the mabl-controlled *policy* — which carriers are permitted — NOT a try-order: order here is not significant. Each host selects the best available protocol from this set (and the fallback order among them) using local signals the operator can't know ahead of time — UDP socket-buffer clamp, an HTTP proxy in the path, live reachability. Set `[mablnet_wss]` to disable QUIC for a tunnel on a known UDP-blocked network, or `[mablnet_quic]` to require QUIC. Only `mablnet_*` values are valid; the worker rebuilds on change. PATCH `null` to clear an override.

mablnet_carrier_connect_timeouts.description: Per-protocol carrier establishment deadline in milliseconds, keyed by `LinkAgentProtocolEnum` value (default `{mablnet_quic: 8000, mablnet_wss: 45000}`): how long the worker waits for a carrier on that protocol to JOIN before falling back to the next protocol the host tries (from `mablnet_allowed_protocols`). The deadline is intrinsic to the protocol — QUIC fast-fails to escape silently-blackholing networks; WSS is patient — and is independent of order. A protocol absent from the map uses the worker's built-in default. PATCH `null` to clear the override.

mablnet_client_pool_size.description: Multi-carrier peer-pool size for CLIENT legs connecting to this tunnel. Deliberately has NO server-side default: unset means each client auto-selects a fixed pool size from its own machine's resources (total memory, capped by cores) — the api can't know them. An explicit value pins the size for every client of the tunnel: `1` = pool off, N > 1 boots N mablnet Hosts per client — one slot identity each, each with its own carriers — and spreads connections across them, lifting the one-pinned-carrier-per-peer throughput cap for many-connection workloads (browser tests). Does not speed up a single bulk stream, and the Link Agent itself is unaffected — this rides to clients on the resolved tunnel (`client_pool_size`). Consumers treat explicit values < 1 as 1; keep N modest (2-4). PATCH `null` to restore client auto-selection.

ready_heartbeat_interval.description: Heartbeat cadence once the Agent reaches `ready` status. While the Agent is still bringing up the legacy / mablnet stacks (status != `ready`) it heartbeats at the hard-coded 10 s tick — fast feedback is what ops + the UI need during startup, and the startup window is short. Once `ready` the cadence drops to this value (default `PT60S`); steady-state Agents mostly only need the heartbeat to guard against sudden death (laptop suspend, network drop) and that doesn't repay 10 s × every Agent in the fleet of api-side load. The Agent reverts to 10 s if `status` ever leaves `ready`. Must stay below the api's dead-agent cleanup threshold (10 min) — `PT300S` (5 min) is a safe upper bound.

agent_log_level.description:
Root logger level. Applied in-place — no Host rebuild.
Deliberately has no server-side default, and should not be given one. The Agent applies this to its process-global root logger on the first announce, which happens *after* it has applied the level from its own config file / command line — so any value set here silently overrides what the customer configured locally. Left unset (the default) the local config stays authoritative; set explicitly, it means an operator chose this level for this tunnel and it wins.

LinkAgentOperatorTunables.description: Operator-tunable parameters for a running Link Agent. Used in two contexts: as the read-only resolved view (`operator_tunables`) and as the sparse overrides (`operator_tunables_overrides`). In the overrides context absent fields fall through to the next merge layer; `null` explicitly clears the override (`x-dao-apply-nulls: true` per-field). In the resolved-view context the api populates every field by merging static defaults (in `LinkLabelServiceImpl`) with label-level overrides and (on `LinkAgent`) agent-level overrides.

recent_errors.description: Fingerprint-deduped ring of the 5 most recent error categories the Agent has seen since process start (or since the last `recent_errors` rotation). Categories — not stack traces or messages — so the field is bounded and PII-safe. Full traces stay in the Agent's local log.

LinkAgentState.description: Rolled-up just-in-time snapshot the Agent pushes on every heartbeat. Snapshot semantics — the api stores only the most recent value as the canonical "current state" view. Trend graphs live in Cloud Monitoring via the mablnet-metrics-collector OTel pipeline; this surface is for incident-triage ergonomics ("show me this Agent's view of the world right now").

carriers_open.description: Number of carriers currently in OPEN state.

carriers.description: The Agent's open carriers, one row per (Router, endpoint) pair — so an Agent holding both a QUIC and a WSS carrier to the same Router reports two rows, and the count of distinct `router_id` values answers "is this Agent multi-homed?". Rows rather than a map keyed by endpoint because behind the load balancer every carrier on a substrate dials the same address, which cannot tell Routers apart. Empty until the worker's first carrier-stats push and once that snapshot goes stale, alongside `carriers_open` reading 0.

peer_count.description: Number of remote peer Hosts the Agent's Host currently knows about.

socks_streams_active.description: Number of inbound SOCKS5 streams currently active (handshake + bridging).

socks_streams_total.description: Total inbound SOCKS5 streams accepted since the process started.

rtt_p50_ms.description: p50 of recent carrier RTT, in milliseconds.

rtt_p99_ms.description: p99 of recent carrier RTT, in milliseconds.

send_window_saturation_pct.description: Share of the last heartbeat window (0-100) during which the Agent's tunnel send path was network-bound — SOCKS sessions sitting at their in-flight write-window high-water mark, i.e. customer data queued behind available tunnel capacity. Computed by the Agent from the worker's cumulative saturation clock; clamped, so overlapping saturated sessions read as fully saturated rather than >100. Sustained high values mean the tunnel itself (not the host) is the constraint — the "add Link Agents" signal. Absent when the Agent or worker predates the signal.

worker_version.description: Version of the native mablnet host worker binary the Agent is currently running. Distinct from the Agent's top-level `version` (the Agent software / distribution version): the worker self-updates on its own channel, so this tracks the running worker generation independently. Absent until the worker has started.

LinkAgentMablnetState.description: Per-Host mablnet snapshot, populated by the Agent from MablnetClient.

router_id.description: The Router these carriers terminate on, and the id the per-carrier debug actions target. Absent when the Agent could not learn it — the carrier is no longer tracked, or the Router advertised none. Not derivable from `endpoint`: behind the load balancer every Router answers on the same address.

endpoint.description: The carrier wire-form the Agent dialed, e.g. `udp://mabl-quic.link.mabl.com:443` or `wss://mabl-wss.link.mabl.com:443/mablnet/v1/carrier`. Identifies the address the customer's network has to allow, not the Router — Routers share it.

protocol.description: Transport carrying this group, `mablnet_quic` or `mablnet_wss`. Reported rather than parsed back out of `endpoint`, so no consumer has to know how a substrate spells its scheme.

LinkAgentCarrier.description: One group of the Agent's open carriers: those terminating on the same Router over the same endpoint. Rebuilt from the worker's live carrier snapshot on every heartbeat, open carriers only.

cpu_utilization_pct.description: Host CPU utilization at the most recent sample, as a percentage (0–100) averaged across all cores.

peak_cpu_utilization_pct.description: Highest CPU-utilization percentage (0–100) observed since the previous heartbeat.

memory_used_bytes.description: Host memory in use at the most recent sample, in bytes.

peak_memory_used_bytes.description: Peak host memory in use since the previous heartbeat, in bytes.

memory_available_bytes.description: Host memory available at the most recent sample, in bytes.

open_fds.description: Open file descriptors held by the worker process at the most recent sample. Each proxied connection consumes one; compare against `os_settings.open_file_limit` for the dominant connection-ceiling headroom.

peak_open_fds.description: Peak worker open file descriptors since the previous heartbeat.

ephemeral_ports_in_use.description: Outbound connections the worker currently holds open, each consuming one ephemeral port — compare against the `os_settings.ephemeral_port_range` size. Counts active connections only; sockets lingering in TIME_WAIT (which still hold a port briefly) are not included.

peak_ephemeral_ports_in_use.description: Peak worker ephemeral-port usage since the previous heartbeat.

connections_rejected.description: Cumulative count, since the worker process started, of outbound dials the worker rejected because a host resource limit was hit (open-file-descriptor or ephemeral-port exhaustion) — not ordinary connection-refused/timeout failures. The unambiguous saturation signal: any nonzero value means the Agent has already turned customer traffic away for want of capacity.

load_average.description: System load average (1-minute) at the most recent sample, from the JVM OperatingSystemMXBean. Compare against `cpu_cores`: a load approaching or exceeding the core count means the run queue is backed up (CPU- or IO-bound) in a way instantaneous CPU% can miss. Absent on Windows (the JVM doesn't expose it there).

swap_used_bytes.description: Swap space in use at the most recent sample, in bytes. Non-zero (and growing) swap use is a memory-pressure signal even when `memory_available_bytes` still looks healthy.

swap_total_bytes.description: Total swap space on the host, in bytes (the denominator for `swap_used_bytes`).

disk_free_bytes.description: Free space, in bytes, on the filesystem holding the Agent's working directory. A full disk breaks worker auto-updates, update staging, and logging.

disk_total_bytes.description: Total size, in bytes, of the filesystem holding the Agent's working directory.

conntrack_count.description: Netfilter connection-tracking entries currently in use at the most recent sample (Linux `nf_conntrack_count`). On a connection-heavy host behind a stateful firewall/NAT, conntrack-table exhaustion drops new connections before any FD/port limit is hit. Absent when the conntrack module isn't loaded.

peak_conntrack_count.description: Peak netfilter conntrack entries observed since the previous heartbeat.

udp_rcvbuf_errors.description: UDP datagrams the kernel dropped for lack of receive-buffer space since the previous heartbeat (Linux `/proc/net/snmp` `Udp: RcvbufErrors`). Read as a trend, not as an attribution: the kernel sums this over **every** UDP socket in the host's network namespace, so it covers the worker's QUIC carrier sockets but also everything else on the box — a browser's QUIC connections, mDNS, a local DNS resolver — and on a general-purpose host those usually dominate it. A nonzero value therefore means inbound UDP throughput is being lost somewhere on the host, not that the carrier lost anything. Correlate with `os_settings.udp_buffer_clamped` before concluding the buffers are too small: that flag is what says a requested socket buffer was actually capped, and it is the only case where raising `net.core.rmem_max` changes the outcome. Absent off Linux.

LinkAgentHostState.description: Host + worker-process resource-utilization snapshot the Agent assembles at heartbeat time. CPU and memory are host-wide, read from the JVM's OperatingSystemMXBean (so they include the worker subprocess); the file-descriptor, ephemeral-port, and connection-rejection counts are the worker process's own, pushed to the Agent over the worker IPC. Current samples plus high-water marks since the previous heartbeat — peaks matter for "how close to its limits" because a periodic sample misses bursts. Pair with the static `cpu_cores` / `total_memory_bytes` / `os_settings` on the Agent for the headroom denominators.

open_file_limit.description: Soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE` — the max open file descriptors the process may hold and the limit that actually binds at runtime. Each proxied connection consumes one. `-1` means unlimited. The common Linux default (1024) is low for a busy tunnel.

open_file_limit_hard.description: Hard `RLIMIT_NOFILE` — the ceiling the soft limit can be raised to without privilege. `-1` means unlimited. When this is also low, raising the soft limit needs a `limits.conf` / systemd change rather than a plain `ulimit -n`.

max_user_processes.description: Soft `RLIMIT_NPROC` — the max processes/threads for the Agent's user. `-1` means unlimited. JVM and worker threads (Netty event loops, etc.) count against it.

ephemeral_port_range_low.description: Low end of `net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range` — the first ephemeral port the kernel hands out to outbound connections. With `ephemeral_port_range_high` it bounds how many simultaneous outbound connections (per remote tuple) the host can open.

socket_recv_buffer_max.description: `net.core.rmem_max` — the max receive socket buffer (bytes) an application may request. Caps carrier throughput on high-latency links when set below what the carrier asks for (the default of ~208 KB is a common bottleneck).

socket_send_buffer_max.description: `net.core.wmem_max` — the max send socket buffer (bytes) an application may request.

udp_recv_buffer_achieved.description: Actual `SO_RCVBUF` (bytes) a UDP socket obtains when it requests the QUIC carrier's target buffer — the post-clamp value `getsockopt` returns, which the kernel caps near `net.core.rmem_max` (and doubles for bookkeeping on Linux). The Agent measures this with a throwaway probe socket, so it is present on every OS (unlike `socket_recv_buffer_max`, which is Linux `/proc`-only). The real signal for whether this host can honor the QUIC carrier's receive flow-control window.

udp_send_buffer_achieved.description: Actual `SO_SNDBUF` (bytes) a UDP socket obtains for the carrier's target request — the send-side counterpart of `udp_recv_buffer_achieved`, capped near `net.core.wmem_max`.

udp_buffer_clamped.description: True when the achieved UDP socket buffer fell materially short of the QUIC carrier's request — i.e. the kernel clamped it (the host needs `net.core.rmem_max` / `wmem_max` raised, or, in a container, the host / WSL2 VM tuned). A clamped buffer throttles QUIC throughput on higher-latency links, so this is the health signal for deciding whether to default this host to the QUIC carrier or fall back to WSS.

conntrack_max.description: `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` — the connection-tracking table size limit, the ceiling for the dynamic `agent_state.host.conntrack_count`. Present only on Linux hosts with the conntrack module loaded (a stateful firewall/NAT); absent otherwise.

LinkAgentOsSettings.description: Static host OS resource limits and network sysctls the Agent reads once at startup (from `/proc` on Linux) and reports on announce. These bind a connection-heavy tunnel well before the mablnet protocol's own stream ceiling: every proxied connection costs a file descriptor and an outbound ephemeral port, so a low open-file limit or a narrow ephemeral-port range caps how many concurrent connections the Agent — and its worker subprocess, which inherits the Agent's rlimits — can carry. Surfaced so operators can audit whether a host is tuned for the Agent's load. Fields are individually omitted when unreadable (e.g. on a non-Linux host), so the object may be sparse or absent.

LinkAgentCapacityStatusEnum.description: Capacity health band, used both for the Agent overall and per resource dimension. `healthy` = comfortable headroom; `warning` = approaching a limit (tune or scale soon); `critical` = at/over a limit, or the Agent has already rejected connections for want of capacity; `unknown` = not enough data yet (no heartbeat carrying host stats). As an OS-warning severity only `warning` / `critical` are used.

LinkAgentCapacityResourceEnum.description: A resource dimension whose live utilization the api compares against its ceiling.

utilization_pct.description: Peak usage as a percentage (0–100) of the ceiling for this dimension.

used.description: Peak raw usage in the dimension's native unit (memory bytes, file-descriptor count, ephemeral-port count). Omitted for `cpu`, whose utilization is already a percentage.

limit.description: Ceiling in the same unit as `used`. Omitted for `cpu`, and when the limit is unbounded (e.g. an unlimited file-descriptor rlimit).

LinkAgentCapacityDimension.description: One resource dimension's peak utilization against its ceiling, derived server-side from the heartbeat `agent_state.host` peaks and the static headroom denominators (`cpu_cores`, `total_memory_bytes`, `os_settings`). Peaks — not instantaneous samples — drive the band, so a burst between heartbeats still registers.

setting.description: The flagged property, and the stable key a client localizes on — one of `open_file_limit`, `ephemeral_port_range`, `socket_buffer_limits`, `host_minimum_memory`, `host_minimum_cpu_cores`, `host_memory`, `link_endpoint_unreachable`. A client that does not recognise a value should skip the advisory: there is no prose here to fall back on.

current.description: The Agent's current value for the setting. Absent for an advisory that is not about a numeric setting at all (`link_endpoint_unreachable`).

recommended.description: The minimum value the api recommends for a busy tunnel. Absent where `current` is.

params.description:
Everything this advisory's copy needs that `current` / `recommended` do not already carry. Keys are stable per `setting`:

* `open_file_limit` — none; `current` and `recommended` are the whole story.
* `ephemeral_port_range` — `low`, `high`: the range endpoints (`current` is its size).
* `socket_buffer_limits` — `variant`: `sysctls_known` when the host's `net.core.rmem_max` / `wmem_max` were readable and the advice can name them, else `sysctls_unknown`. The two texts differ in structure rather than in values, so a client selects between them (i18next: pass it as `context`) rather than interpolating. Both reproduce from `recommended`; nothing about the remediation needs prose from the api.
* `host_minimum_memory` — none; `current` and `recommended` (the minimum) are in MiB. Always `critical`: the Agent cannot run its mablnet worker on such a host.
* `host_minimum_cpu_cores` — none; `current` and `recommended` (the minimum) are cores.
* `host_memory` — `tunnels`: how many tunnels the host runs, the multiplier behind `recommended`.
* `link_endpoint_unreachable` — `quic_endpoint` / `wss_endpoint`: the `host:port` the Agent could not reach, present only for an endpoint it actually attempted (a mabl-bound HTTP proxy suppresses the QUIC carrier entirely, and naming an endpoint the Agent never dialled would send the customer after the wrong firewall rule). The Agent's own account of the failure is on `connection_status[*].last_error`. Plus `variant`: `fallback_available` when the Agent is reporting a working legacy `wss` connection to carry traffic over meanwhile, `no_fallback` when it is not — either because the tunnel is mablnet-only or because the Agent cannot reach anything at all. The two consequences are different sentences, so a client selects between them (i18next: `context`) rather than interpolating. The transport belongs to the key, not a param: `quic_endpoint` is UDP, `wss_endpoint` is TCP.

LinkAgentOsWarning.description:
Something about the Agent's host or network that needs the customer's action — an OS setting (`open_file_limit`, `ephemeral_port_range`, `socket_buffer_limits`), a host below the published minimums (`host_minimum_memory`, `host_minimum_cpu_cores`), the host's memory against the tunnels it runs (`host_memory`), or a mabl endpoint the Agent cannot reach (`link_endpoint_unreachable`). Advisory — it flags a condition the customer can fix, distinct from a dimension's live `status` (which reflects actual utilization). Thresholds live in the api; see the capacity-insights design doc.

`setting` is a stable key, and `current` / `recommended` / `params` carry every value the copy needs, so a client renders its own localized string from them. There is deliberately no prose here: the api has no request locale, so anything it composed would be English for every reader, and a second copy of a sentence the client owns is only somewhere for the two to drift apart. A client is therefore expected to ship copy for a `setting` before — or with — the api starts sending it, and to skip an advisory whose key it does not recognise.

dimensions.description: Per-resource utilization-vs-ceiling, one entry per computable dimension.

os_warnings.description: Conditions on the Agent's host or network the customer should act on — OS settings below recommended values, the host's memory against the tunnels it runs, and mabl endpoints the Agent cannot reach. Empty when the host is well-tuned, adequately sized, and reaching mabl.

supported_tunnels.description:
How many tunnels this host's memory supports — a projection, not a limit the api enforces, and not a health signal: it is informational even when the Agent runs fewer. Pair it with `tunnels_on_host` to render "running 4 of 14".

Derived from `total_memory_bytes` alone, allowing for the Agent process and for the extra worker an update runs alongside the others, since each tunnel runs its own worker process. It therefore assumes the host is dedicated to the Agent — a host also running a database supports fewer, which the `memory` dimension's live utilization is what reveals. Absent when the Agent reported no memory total, and `0` for a host too small for even one tunnel.

Capped at 64 however much memory the host has. Memory is the only term measured, and on a large host it is not the binding one — core count, the file-descriptor limit and the ephemeral-port range bite first, and turning those into a tunnel count needs data we do not have. Those limits are reported separately instead: as `open_file_limit` and `ephemeral_port_range` advisories, and as the live `cpu` dimension.

LinkAgentCapacity.description: Server-derived capacity insights, recomputed on every read (never persisted) from the heartbeat `agent_state.host` utilization peaks, the static headroom denominators (`cpu_cores`, `total_memory_bytes`, `os_settings`), and the `connections_rejected` saturation counter. Answers "how close is this Agent to its limits, and is its host tuned?" for the capacity-insights UI. Present once the Agent has announced its memory total — enough for the `supported_tunnels` projection — with the utilization dimensions filling in from its first heartbeat carrying host stats.

timestamp.description: Last time the Agent saw an error matching this fingerprint.

fingerprint.description: Stable category for this error (e.g. `carrier-connect-failed`, `peer-ca-fetch-401`, `mablnet-host-rebuild`). Categories, not stack traces — kept narrow so the field stays bounded across noisy upstreams.

count.description: Number of distinct errors that mapped to this fingerprint in the window.

request_id.description: Opaque caller-supplied identifier (recommended: ULID). Agent dedupes by this value and surfaces it back on the ack.

action.description: Discriminator. Each value maps to a typed sub-schema with that action's argument shape.

requested_at.description: When the api enqueued this request.

requested_by.description: Operator identifier (e.g. mabl user id). Audit-only — not used for authorization.

LinkAgentOperatorDebugRequest.description: Operator-issued debug request, queued by the api on the LinkAgent and pulled by the Agent on its next poll. Discriminated by `action`; each variant has its own arg shape. Idempotent by design — the Agent dedupes by `request_id` (an LRU of the last 64 ids in-process), so the api re-sending a pending request after an Agent restart is a no-op rather than a re-execute.

LinkAgentDumpStateRequest.description: Tell the Agent to dump its full in-memory state (Host, carriers, peers, active SOCKS streams) to its local log at INFO. No arguments.

LinkAgentRedialCarriersRequest.description: Retire + reopen every carrier on the Agent's Host. Useful when LB topology changes and the Agent is stuck on stale Routers. No arguments.

LinkAgentRedialCarrierRequest.description: Single-carrier variant of `redial-carriers`. Targets one Router id (which the heartbeat's `agent_state.mablnet.carriers` rows report).

router_id.description: Router id to redial. Matches a `router_id` in `agent_state.mablnet.carriers`.

LinkAgentForcePeerCaRefetchRequest.description: Bypass the Agent's MablnetPeerCaClient backoff and fetch the peer-CA bundle immediately. Used during peer-CA rotation incidents. No arguments.

LinkAgentSyntheticDialRequest.description: Have the Agent attempt an inbound SOCKS5 dial through its own service to the specified target (resolves and dials on the Agent side, in the customer network). Used to verify customer-internal reachability during incident triage.

target_host.description: Hostname or IP the Agent should dial.

outcome.description: Agent-side outcome. `skipped-duplicate` = Agent saw this id in its recent-requests LRU and short-circuited; `unknown-action` = Agent's version of the schema doesn't know the requested action (older Agent + newer api).

detail.description: Free-form additional context. PII-sanitised on the Agent side — categories and identifiers only, no payload contents.

completed_at.description: When the Agent finished executing this request.

LinkAgentOperatorDebugResult.description: Agent → api ack for a previously-issued debug request. The api matches by `request_id`, marks the queued request as completed, and surfaces the result to whoever issued it. The api drops the queued request once the ack lands so the Agent doesn't have to re-send results on subsequent heartbeats.

id.description: UUID for this Link Agent instance

created_time.description: Time at which the Link Agent was created

created_by_id.description: The principal that registered this Link Agent — normally the API key the agent runs under. Server-set from the authenticated caller; supplying it is ignored. Activity feed attribution reads this, so an agent without it is reported as having been registered by mabl itself.

last_updated_time.description: Time at which the Link Agent record last changed

last_updated_by_id.description: The principal behind the most recent change to this Link Agent — the API key for a status change reported by the agent, or the user who started or ended a maintenance window. Server-set from the authenticated caller; supplying it is ignored.

deleted_time.description: Time at which the Link Agent was stopped or removed

last_heartbeat_time.description: Time at which the Link Agent last sent a heartbeat

version.description: The version of the Link Agent software that this instance is running

update_available.description: Whether a newer Link Agent release than this agent's version is available for download. Computed for the Java distribution only — the mabl-cli distribution self-updates via its own channels and its version is not comparable to Java releases. Server-computed on read; absent when it cannot be determined (the mabl-cli distribution, an unknown or unparseable agent version, or the release inventory being unavailable).

latest_available_version.description: The newest released Link Agent version, present whenever update_available is computed

label.description: The user-provided label for this Link Agent instance

point_of_contact.description: Optional point of contact (a name or email address) for this Link Agent, supplied by the operator via config file or command-line at startup. Surfaced so support can tell who to contact about a given Agent. Free-form — not validated as an email.

no_ssl_verify.description: Flag indicating whether the agent was started with SSL verification disabled

tunnel_port.description: DEPRECATED - Not used as of Link 2.0

hostname.description: The Link Agent instance's local hostname

machine_identity.description: Opaque persisted per-machine identity — a mabl-minted UUID stored in the standard OS-specific mabl config directory — required when announcing a personal (`user`-owned) tunnel. The server derives the tunnel's label from it (SHA-256 of `machine_identity ":" link_infrastructure_key`, lowercase hex, truncated to the 24-char label limit), so one machine keeps one stable tunnel identity per cluster across restarts, reboots, and hostname changes. Not used for workspace- or company-owned agents.

link_infrastructure_key.description: On request, personal (`user`-owned) announces only: the explicit placement choice when the user's workspace associations resolve to more than one link infrastructure — the ambiguous announce fails with an error naming the candidate keys, and the shared cluster's key is always a valid choice. Omit when the associations are unambiguous. Ignored on requests for workspace- and company-owned agents. On response, for every agent: the link infrastructure key of the dedicated cluster this agent's tunnel is on, omitted on the shared cluster (absent means shared). A personal tunnel reports its recorded placement; a workspace or company agent its owning company's current key, which changes when the company moves between clusters. An agent fetches its peer-CA bundle for this key (`GET /link/mablnet/peer-ca?infrastructure_key=`).

address.description: The Link Agent instance's local IP address

java_version.description: Value of the 'java.version' Java system property

java_vm_name.description: Value of the 'java.vm.name' Java system property

operating_system_architecture.description: Value of the 'os.arch' Java system property

operating_system_name.description: Value of the 'os.name' Java system property

operating_system_version.description: Value of the 'os.version' Java system property

cpu_cores.description: Number of CPU cores available to the Agent host — the headroom denominator for CPU utilization.

total_memory_bytes.description: Total physical memory on the Agent host, in bytes — the headroom denominator for memory utilization.

tunnels_on_host.description: How many tunnels this Agent process supervises, as the Agent itself counts them. Every mablnet tunnel runs its own worker process, so this is the multiplier on the host's memory requirement — the api pairs it with `total_memory_bytes` to flag an undersized host. Each of a multi-tunnel process's Agent records reports the same value. Reported by the Agent rather than derived from records sharing a hostname, which containers and cloned VM images make unreliable. Absent from Agents predating the field.

protocols.description: The set of protocols this Link Agent is currently attempting to keep connections open for. Successor to the singular `protocol` field. A dual-stack Agent during the mablnet migration reports both `wss` (legacy Link Tunnel) and one of the `mablnet_*` values; mabl ops watches this set to determine which accounts are migration-eligible.

capabilities.description: Optional behaviors this Link Agent supports. Reported by the Agent at startup. Operator endpoints that depend on Agent-side handling (`POST /link/agents/{id}/maintenance`, etc.) reject requests when the relevant capability is missing — older Agents that predate the capability simply omit it.

is_connected.description: DEPRECATED: legacy single-protocol connection state. Agents reporting `protocols` populate `endpoints` with per-protocol connection state; this field stays populated as `true` if any of the per-protocol states are connected.

current_link_server_id.description: DEPRECATED: legacy single-Link-Server binding. Mablnet Agents are not bound to a single Server — they multi-home across Routers. Stays populated for legacy Agents.

current_link_server_endpoint.description: DEPRECATED: legacy single-endpoint field. Use `endpoints[wss].address` for the same value; the legacy field stays populated for pre-mablnet Agents that don't yet understand the `endpoints` map.

endpoints.description:
Per-protocol endpoint the Link Agent should connect to, keyed by protocol name (matches `LinkAgentProtocolEnum`). Legacy Link Tunnel Agents only see (and need) the `wss` entry, which mirrors `current_link_server_endpoint`. Mablnet-capable Agents additionally see `mablnet_wss` and (when UDP/QUIC is exposed externally) `mablnet_quic`, pointing at the Application LB FQDN for this environment.
api-set and read-only from the client perspective: the value flows api → Agent. Per-protocol connection health flowing the other direction (Agent → api) is reported via `connection_status`.
Computed on every read from the LinkLabel + workspace migration flags + deployment config (`com.mabl.mablnet.domain` + the owner's link infrastructure key); NOT persisted on the LinkAgent itself. A feature-flag flip, FQDN change, or LinkLabel-level update propagates to running Agents on their next poll (≈ 10 s), with no agent restart and no backfill cron. Downstream consumers that need the same view (BigQuery, Pub/Sub) should read via the api rather than the raw DAO entity.

connection_status.description: Per-protocol connection health, keyed by protocol name (same keys as `endpoints`). Reported by the Agent on heartbeat and merged in.

mablnet_tenant_id.description: Denormalised view of `LinkLabel.mablnet_tenant_id` for this Agent's label. Computed on every read alongside `endpoints` (see that field's description for the full server-set-fields contract); NOT persisted on the LinkAgent. Tenant ids themselves are immutable for a LinkLabel's lifetime, so the value is stable across reads in practice.

mablnet_tenant_id_hex.description: Zero-padded 8-character lowercase hex form of `mablnet_tenant_id`, e.g. `bee85e2b`. Provided for log/grep/observability ergonomics; the numeric and hex forms always agree (both computed together). Same lifecycle as `mablnet_tenant_id` — computed on every read, not persisted.

status.description: The current status of the Link Agent

operator_debug_queue.description: Debug requests queued by mabl ops for this Agent to execute on its next poll. Bounded — the api rejects enqueues that would exceed `maxItems`. The Agent drains entries on its next tick, executes idempotently (and short-circuits any `request_id` it's seen recently), and acks the outcome via `operator_debug_results` on the next heartbeat. The api drops the matching queue entry on ack so the queue stays self-draining.

operator_debug_results.description: Acks pushed by the Agent on heartbeat for previously-queued debug requests. The api matches by `request_id`, drops the matching queue entry, and surfaces the outcome to whichever caller originally enqueued the request.

workspace_id.description: The workspace that owns this Link Agent, for `workspace`-owned tunnels. Unset for `company`-owned agents (mablnet-only) — read `owner_type`/`owner_id` for the canonical scope.

owner_id.description: The id of the owning entity — equals `workspace_id` for `workspace`-owned agents, the company id for `company`-owned agents.

LinkAgent.description: Represents a single instance of a running Link Agent

http_proxy.description: The configured upstream HTTP CONNECT proxy as `host:port`. Credentials, if any, are omitted — see `proxy_auth_configured`. Absent when no fixed proxy is configured.

proxy_pac_url.description: The proxy auto-configuration (PAC) URL the Agent evaluates to pick a proxy per destination, when PAC-based proxying is configured. Absent for fixed-proxy or no-proxy setups.

proxy_exclusions.description: Destinations that bypass the proxy and are dialed directly — suffix, IPv4, IPv6, or CIDR expressions.

proxy_auth_configured.description: Whether proxy credentials (fixed-proxy or PAC) are configured. The credentials themselves are never reported; this flag lets support confirm auth is present when diagnosing a 407 from the customer's proxy.

mablnet_update_channel.description: The release channel this Agent pulls its mablnet worker binary from — e.g. `stable`, `latest`, or a `branch:<name>` channel.

link_agent_update_channel.description: The release channel this Agent updates *itself* from — e.g. `stable` (the default, published only when the Agent is tagged), `latest` (every build of the Agent's trunk), a major version such as `3`, or a branch channel. The counterpart of `mablnet_update_channel`, which governs the worker binary rather than the Agent.

auto_updates_enabled.description: Whether the Agent applies mablnet worker auto-updates.

tunnels.description: The unique set of tunnel names served by this same Agent process. A single Agent instance can serve several tunnels; every one of that instance's LinkAgent records reports the same set, so any one of them shows the full picture.

log_level.description: The Agent's configured logging level. Support diagnostics.

max_concurrent_connections.description: Configured cap on concurrent tunnel connections. Support diagnostics.

max_connection_attempts.description: Configured cap on connection retry attempts. Support diagnostics.

shutdown_drain_timeout_seconds.description: How long the Agent drains in-flight work on shutdown before exiting. Support diagnostics.

mablnet_router.description: The configured mablnet Router endpoint override as `host:port`, if any. Support diagnostics.

mablnet_peer_ca_path.description: Filesystem path to the mablnet peer CA override, if configured. Support diagnostics.

mablnet_update_pull_interval_seconds.description: How often the Agent polls for a new mablnet worker build, in seconds. Support diagnostics.

LinkAgentConfiguration.description: A Link Agent's effective, credential-free runtime configuration. Populated by both the Java Link Agent (the full surface below) and the mabl-cli Link Agent (its narrower carrier/uplink surface); fields the reporting Agent has no value for are omitted. Never carries secrets — proxy, PAC, and tunnel credentials are represented only by the `proxy_auth_configured` boolean. The first group of fields is surfaced to customers on the Link Agent details view; the rest is support-oriented detail.

mode.description: `allow` — only listed destinations are reachable; `deny` — listed destinations are refused and all others allowed; `disabled` — no filtering, every destination allowed.

destinations.description: The host/port rules the mode applies to — `host`, `host:port`, `:port`, IPv4/IPv6 literals, and CIDR ranges (IPv6 bracketed as `[addr]:port`).

LinkAgentConnectionFilter.description: A Link Agent's destination allow/deny connection policy.

exclusions.description: Destinations that bypass this proxy and are dialed directly.

LinkAgentUpstreamProxy.description: A fixed upstream HTTP CONNECT proxy applied to customer-test-target dials, with its bypass list. Credentials are never included.

LinkAgentProxyMode.description: Which classes of the Agent's traffic route through the configured HTTP proxy: `all` — both the mabl control-plane connection and customer-test-target traffic; `mabl` — only the Agent's connection to mabl; `upstream` — only customer-test-target traffic; `none` — no proxy.

link_agents.description: All Link Agents that matched the query

link_server_id.description: The ID of the Link Server

host.description: The Link Server host (hostname or IP address) for SSL connections

port.description: The Link Server port for SSL connections

fqdn.description: The fully qualified domain name of the Link Server

client_certificate.description: The serialized client certificate to use when connecting to the server

server_fingerprint.description: The fingerprint of the server that should be expected when connecting

server_public_key.description: The public key of the server

LinkServerConnection.description: Contains information that the Link Agent should use to connect to a Link Server

LinkMigrationPhaseEnum.description: Where a workspace is in the Link 2.0 to 3.0 migration. link_2_only, link_3_partially_installed and link_3_installed are before Link 3.0 is enabled, split by how many live Agents run a Link 3.0 capable version. link_3_blocked, link_3_upgrade_pending and link_3_ready have Link 3.0 enabled with test runs still on Link 2.0: blocked when a Link 3.0 capable Agent lacks a Link 3.0 connection, upgrade_pending when only Agents on Link 2.x do, and ready when every live Agent has one. tests_on_link_3 and link_3_only (Link 2.0 retired) route test runs over Link 3.0, each with an unhealthy variant when a live Agent lacks a Link 3.0 connection. misconfigured flags route test runs over a Link version the Agents are not told to use.

LinkMigrationFlagSourceEnum.description: Where a Link migration flag is turned on, if anywhere

last_error.description: The Agent's most recent Link 3.0 connection error, if it reported one

LinkMigrationBlockingAgent.description: A live Link Agent without a Link 3.0 connection that blocks its workspace's next migration step

held.description: The account excludes link_protocol_mablnet, which marks it as not to be migrated by fleet tooling

native_link_3.description: The account was created on Link 3.0 rather than migrated to it

link_protocol_tunnel.description: Whether link_protocol_tunnel is on, from the account or the workspace's labs

link_3_capable_agent_count.description: Live Agents running a Link 3.0 capable version

link_3_connected_agent_count.description: Live Agents with a working Link 3.0 connection

LinkMigrationWorkspace.description: One workspace's Link 2.0 to 3.0 migration status

LinkMigrationWorkspaceList.description: The Link 2.0 to 3.0 migration status of every workspace with a live Link Agent

node_id.description: Unique identifier for the node (server-generated, suffix -kgn)

workspace_id.description: The workspace this node belongs to

application_id.description: The application this node is associated with

summary.description: A short summary of the concept

content.description: Detailed content for this node (max 20K chars before embedding fallback)

confidence.description: Confidence score (0.0-1.0) mapped from tier (high=1.0, medium=0.6, low=0.3)

provenance_summary.description: Free-text provenance summary for this concept

properties.description: Additional structured properties for this node

embedding_input_is_summary.description: True if embedding was computed from summary rather than content (content exceeded 20K chars)

version.description: Monotonic edit counter (server-managed, readOnly)

substring_rank.description: 1-based rank in the substring branch from the RRF fusion. When no match is found, the endpoint returns HTTP 204 No Content with no body — callers should treat 204 as "no name match".
