status_names.description: Zephyr test execution status names mabl records outcomes as. Each must exist, and not be archived, in every configured project. passed and failed are saved as Pass and Fail when unset at create.

environment_mapping.description: How mabl environments map to Zephyr environments. Saved as by_name when unset at create.

attach_screenshots.description: Attach the failure screenshot to failed executions. Saved as true when unset at create.

auto_sync_enabled.description: When true, mabl records each completed plan run's results in Zephyr without a manual sync request. Ad hoc runs and plan runs whose tests carry no Zephyr case keys are skipped. Unset reads as false; an update that omits it keeps the saved value.

token_expires_at.description: UTC epoch milliseconds at which the saved API token expires, read from the token when it is saved, for display only. Absent when the token carries no expiry. Set by mabl; ignored on writes.

zephyr.description: Configuration for a Zephyr Cloud integration. The API token goes in authentication.api_key. On update, omitted fields keep their saved values and the saved token is reused when api_key is omitted; the resulting integration is revalidated against Zephyr.

organization_url.description: Base URL of the Azure DevOps organization, e.g. https://dev.azure.com/contoso. Validated as an exact dev.azure.com authority with an organization path segment; request URLs are built from the validated components rather than by concatenating this string.

project_id.description: GUID of the Azure DevOps project this integration is bound to. Source of truth for the project; project_name is display only.

project_name.description: Display name of the Azure DevOps project, captured when the project is selected. A display convenience only - project_id remains the source of truth, and this value may be stale if the project is renamed in Azure DevOps.

default_work_item_type.description: Name of the work item type created by default, e.g. Bug -- the name Azure's endpoints address types by, not the reference name. Users may still pick another type the project defines. Validated against the project's types when supplied.

work_item_types.description: Per work item type settings for mabl's create-issue form. Written wholesale: an update that omits this keeps the stored list, an empty list clears it, and any other list replaces it. Cleared when the organization or project changes unless supplied in the same update.

subscription_ids.description: Service hook subscription IDs mabl provisioned for this integration, retained so they can be removed when the integration is disabled, deleted, or re-pointed at a different organization or project.

mark_linked_test_cases_automated.description: When true, mabl marks the Azure Test Cases its tests link (AB#123 or a work item URL) as Automated by writing their associated automation fields, and clears its own marker once no test links the case. Automation another tool set is never changed. Unset reads as false; an update that omits it keeps the saved value.

decision.description: Whether the request is approved or denied.

note.description: Why, at most 500 characters; shown with the approval.

GuardrailApprovalDecisionInput.description: A person's decision on a pending approval.

id.description: The approval's id, which the agent sends back in the X-Mabl-Approval header.

workspace_id.description: The id of the workspace the request was made in.

action.description: The action the request asks for, e.g. Delete::Branch.

operation_id.description: The API operation the request called.

resource_type.description: The kind of entity the action acts on, e.g. Branch.

resource_id.description: The id of the entity the request names, when it names one.

branch.description: The branch the request names, when it names one.

request_fields.description: The fields of the request body shown to the approver, as the agent sent them, keyed by property, e.g. name. Some, such as a merge's from and to, also bind the approval. Absent when the operation names none or the body has none. Each value is a string; a long one is shown cut short but bound in full.

agent_type.description: The type of agent that made the request.

agent_session_id.description: The agent session that made the request; absent for an external agent, which has none.

client_kind.description: For an external agent, the kind of client it connected through, e.g. mcp.

policy_ids.description: The ids of the policies that asked for approval.

reason.description: Why the deciding policy asks for approval, as its author wrote it.

summary.description: What the agent asked to do, written by mabl from the request.

decision_id.description: The id of the guardrail decision that asked for approval, in the decision log.

created_by_id.description: The id of the person or API key the agent acts for.

created_time.description: When the agent asked.

request_expires_time.description: When a pending approval expires undecided.

decided_by_id.description: The id of the person who approved or denied it.

decided_time.description: When it was approved, denied or cancelled.

decision_note.description: The note the deciding person left.

use_expires_time.description: Until when the agent may repeat the approved request, as often as it does.

last_updated_by_id.description: The id of whoever last changed the approval.

last_updated_time.description: When the approval last changed.

url.description: The mabl app page where the approval is reviewed.

GuardrailApproval.description: A request an agent made that a guardrail policy asks a person to approve, bound to that agent and to the request's operation, action, path and query parameters and the operation's declared key fields; other body content is not bound. Timestamps are epoch milliseconds.

GuardrailRuleEffect.description: What happens when the rule matches: ALLOW lets the action run, ASK requires a person's approval, BLOCK refuses it with the rule's reason, or with a mabl-written one naming the rule's target when the rule has none. The strictest matching rule wins, so an ALLOW never overrides another rule's or mabl's refusal.

GuardrailRuleKind.description: How the rule is decided. RULE matches on the action and the request's attributes; it is the only kind a rule can have.

GuardrailRuleSetMode.description: Whether a rule set's effects reach agents. ENFORCE applies every rule in the set wherever the workspace enforces guardrails; PREVIEW evaluates and logs every rule without ever changing what the agent gets.

GuardrailRuleTargetType.description: The kind of thing a rule applies to. ACTION is one action such as Delete::Flow, GROUP a catalog group of actions such as destructive, SCOPE every action under a permission scope such as write:flows.

GuardrailRiskGroup.description: How much an action can change. READ only reads, CHANGE creates or edits, COSTLY runs work that consumes credits or capacity, DESTRUCTIVE deletes, merges or restores.

type.description: Whether id names an action, a group or a scope.

id.description: The id of the action (e.g. Delete::Flow), group (e.g. destructive) or scope (e.g. write:flows), as the catalog lists it.

GuardrailRuleTarget.description: The action, group of actions or scope a rule applies to.

GuardrailConditionOp.description: How a condition tests its attribute against its values. eq and neq compare with the one value, in and not_in with any of the values, prefix checks whether the attribute starts with any of the values, and exists checks whether the request carries the attribute at all and takes no values.

attribute.description: The request attribute a test checks: action.id, action.verb, action.resource, action.scope, principal.root, agent.caller, context.branch or resource.id. agent.caller is external for a coding agent connected over MCP or the CLI and mabl for mabl's own agents.

op.description: How a test checks its attribute.

values.description: What a test compares the attribute with; absent for exists, exactly one for eq and neq.

all.description: A combination that holds when every one of its conditions holds; never empty.

any.description: A combination that holds when at least one of its conditions holds; never empty.

GuardrailCondition.description: When a rule applies. Either a test, which sets attribute, op and values and nothing else, or a combination, which sets exactly one of all or any and nothing else. Combinations nest at most four deep. Example: {attribute: context.branch, op: eq, values: [master]}.

id.description: The id of the existing rule this entry keeps, preserving its creation; absent for a new rule.

target.description: What the rule applies to; must be in the catalog.

effect.description: What happens to an agent request the rule matches.

condition.description: Narrows the rule to the requests it matches; absent when the rule always applies.

reason.description: Why the rule exists, shown to the agent and person it refuses, at most 500 characters. When absent, a refusal says the workspace's guardrails block the rule's target.

flow_invariant_id.description: The invariant ID of the flow

flow_preconditions.description: The GenAI summary of the flow preconditions

labels.description: User provided labels on the flow.

distance.description:
Cosine distance between the query embedding and the flow's task embedding.

last_updated_time.description:
When the flow was last edited. Derived from the creation time of the latest
flow variant (every flow edit creates a new variant).

flow_type.description: Type of flow. Set at create and immutable afterwards: the value sent to either PATCH is ignored, and a create that omits it is classified from the step content the request carries.

reusable.description: Indicates whether this can be used by multiple tests

name.description:
The display name of the flow. Required (non-blank) for reusable flows.
When absent on older reusable data, the API serves the description value
here; non-reusable flows are never given a name they did not have.

description.description:
Usage notes and considerations for the flow. Historically this field held
the flow's display name; that role has moved to `name`. To rename a flow,
write `name` — writing this field edits the description only. When a flow
has no description, the API serves the flow's name here for backwards
compatibility.

source_control_tags.description: mapping of tags to version numbers the tag is currently applied to

import_source_version.description: Version of the import tool used to import this flow

minimize_execution_overhead.description:
When enabled, mabl will not capture screenshots, network logs, DOM snapshots,
or other test artifacts in order to report the most accurate flow execution time

reuse_browser_state_in_plan_run.description:
Shares the browser state this flow produces with the rest of a cloud plan run.

Tests that reach the flow before any state has been stored each run it and store
their own result. The tests in a plan stage start together, so that is the common
case; a test that starts once state already exists for the same application and
credentials begins from that stored state instead.

To sign in once per plan run, put a test that runs this flow in an earlier plan
stage, against the same application URL and with the same credentials. Stages run
in order, so the tests of later stages all start from the state that test stored.

A marked flow still runs every time. It is not skipped, so it must decide for
itself whether there is anything left to do — a login flow, for example, should
wrap its sign-in steps in a condition that only holds when the login page is
actually showing. A marked flow that unconditionally repeats its work will do so
on a browser that already carries the session.

The stored state lasts only for the plan run. Has no effect on local CLI runs.

FlowSearchTypeEnum.description:
External flow-type filter for flow search. "browser" selects standard browser flows
(internal flow_type "mablscript"); legacy browser flow types are not present in the
search surface and are not matched.

query.description:
Token query. Multi-token defaults to AND; join with " OR " to broaden
recall (e.g., "login OR signin OR authentication"). Adjacent tokens are
treated as a phrase. Empty query returns zero rows.

search_field.description:
Which tokenized column to search. "combined" searches
name+description+steps+task_summary+labels plus api flow url, parameter-name/value,
and assertion text. Use a single field name to scope to one column. "name" is the
flow's display name; "description" holds its usage notes (on flows that predate the
name field, the name may still live there). "api_endpoint" scopes to api_steps request URL paths and
"api_parameters" to api_steps request parameter names, each optionally paired with
a truncated value (e.g. a search for "42" can match a "customerId" parameter valued
"42"); both match api-type flows only — browser/mobile flows never match on them
("steps" covers their annotated step text), and flow input parameters are not
searched. All fields match whole words (relevance-ranked); partial-word fragments
do not match.

application_id.description:
Optional. When set, returns flows used by at least one test that resolves
to this application (plan membership, training-time application, or recent
run history), plus reusable flows used by no test at all (returned with
usage_count 0); flows used only by tests that resolve to a different
application are excluded. Tests with no discoverable application
association are treated as in-scope (the same resolution
application-scoped test search uses), so flows used only by such tests
stay findable. usage_count reflects usage within this application.

label_filter.description:
Exact-match label filter. When set, only flows whose `labels` array
contains every entry in this list are returned. Max 20 entries.

updated_after.description:
Optional. Only return flows edited at or after this timestamp. Backed by the
creation time of the flow's latest variant (every flow edit creates a new
variant).

include_non_reusable.description:
When true, include non-reusable flows (inline test-step fragments) in the
results. These rows rarely have descriptions and are sparsely indexed, so
the default excludes them.

limit.description: Per-call hard limit. Capped at 200 server-side.

FlowReferenceTextSearchRequest.description:
Parameters for token-based full-text search over `flow_reference` using the
Spanner SEARCH() function and `idx_flow_reference_search_v3`.

matches.description: Flows matching the query, ordered by SCORE(combined_tokens, query) descending.

truncated.description:
True if any match's steps_text was trimmed by the server-side character cap.
Derived from the per-match steps_truncated flags.

description.description: The flow's usage notes and considerations. On flows that predate the name field this may still hold the display name.

task_summary.description: GenAI-generated summary of what the flow does.

precondition_summary.description: GenAI-generated summary of the state the flow requires before running.

usage_count.description: Number of tests using this flow.

last_updated_time.description:
When the flow was last edited. Derived from the creation time of the latest
flow variant.

steps_text.description:
The flow's step content. Annotated step descriptions for browser/mobile
flows; the api_steps JSON for api-type flows (which have no annotated
steps). Server caps the text at a defensive character limit; the calling
agent service applies its own adaptive truncation on top.

steps_truncated.description: True when steps_text was trimmed by the server-side character cap.

score.description: Spanner SCORE(combined_tokens, query). Higher = better. Not bounded above.

matched_field.description:
The field where the match landed when search_field is not "combined".
"api_endpoint" and "api_parameters" only ever appear for api-type flows.

query.description:
Search input. Short keyword-style ("login flow") or longer natural-language
("reusable flow that fills out the checkout shipping form") are both fine.
As a special case, if the input contains one or more flow ids, the endpoint
resolves those ids directly (a direct lookup) and returns the matching flows
without running the search agent. This id fast-path intentionally bypasses
application_id and filters — a pasted id is a request for that exact flow,
not a search — while workspace scope is still enforced.

context.description:
Optional additional context, e.g., a code-change overview from a
calling coding agent. Wrapped in <ADDITIONAL_CONTEXT> for the LLM.

application_id.description:
When set, BOTH search tools (text and semantic) return flows used by at
least one test that resolves to this application (plan membership,
training-time application, or recent run history; tests with no
discoverable application association are included as a fallback, matching
application-scoped test search), plus reusable flows used by no test at
all (returned with usage_count 0). The agent does not receive
application_id as a tool parameter; it's applied automatically.

Flows have no direct application association (scoping is via the tests
that use the flow), so flows used only by tests that resolve to a
different application are excluded; flows used by no test at all remain
searchable. Omit it to search all reusable flows in the workspace.

limit.description:
Maximum number of flows to return after synthesis. The service currently
returns at most 50 regardless of this value: a request above 50 is not
rejected, only silently clamped to 50, so callers already sending a higher
value (up to the schema maximum below) keep working.

include_details.description:
When true, each returned match also includes `steps` — the flow's step
content (annotated step descriptions for browser/mobile flows; the
api_steps JSON for api-type flows), truncated to the per-flow
adaptive-truncation budget (at step boundaries for browser/mobile flows;
by character cap for api-type flows), with `steps_truncated` flagging
when it was trimmed. Present only for flows a search tool surfaced (the
id fast-path carries none — getFlow does not return the search surface's
annotated step text). Off by default to keep responses lean for callers
(e.g. UI) that only need the lightweight summaries. Adds no extra lookups
— the step text is gathered during the normal search round and would
otherwise be discarded.

FlowSearchRequest.description:
Inputs for the flow-search agent. The `query` field accepts both terse
keyword-style inputs and longer natural-language descriptions; the agent
decides how to phrase each tool call internally.

flow_type.description: Optional filter on flow type. Unlike test search, api flows are fully searchable (their task summaries and embeddings are populated).

labels.description: Exact-match label filter; flows must contain ALL listed labels. Capped at 20 entries — both search modalities enforce every listed label (the text tool in SQL, the semantic tool via post-filter), so a request with more labels is rejected rather than silently truncated.

updated_after.description: Only return flows edited at or after this timestamp. Backed by the creation time of the flow's latest variant (every flow edit creates a new variant).

FlowSearchFilters.description:
Structural filters enforced server-side on the search results. application_id
lives at the request top level (not here) because both tools always honor it.
The fields below are applied by the service regardless of how the agent phrases
its tool calls, so returned flows always comply with them. The one exception is
the id fast-path (see the query field): a direct lookup by flow id bypasses
these filters and application_id.

relevance_reason.description: One sentence explaining why this flow matches the input (max ~300 chars).

matched_via.description:
The agent's attribution of which search modality(ies) make this flow
relevant. This is the agent's judgment, not a mechanical record of which
tool returned the row.

task_summary.description: GenAI-generated summary of what the flow does.

precondition_summary.description: GenAI-generated summary of the state the flow requires before running.

flow_type.description: External flow type. All browser-based internal flow types map to browser.

mobile_platform.description: Mobile platform when the flow type is mobile.

usage_count.description: Number of tests using this flow. A reuse signal for ranking.

last_updated_time.description:
When the flow was last edited. Derived from the creation time of the latest
flow variant.

steps.description:
The flow's step content: annotated step descriptions for browser/mobile
flows, the api_steps JSON for api-type flows. Truncated at step boundaries
to the per-flow adaptive-truncation budget; when trimmed, ends with

TestSelection.description: An explicit set of tests to run for a deployment, in place of matching stored plans by label. mabl runs them as one synthesized plan whose identity is scoped to the event, so the runs appear on the deployment results page like any other deployment run. Supports browser or API tests, without mixing types. Each test runs at its version on the selection's mabl branch, falling back to master when it has none there. That branch is the event's branch (or source_control_tag), else the deployment's branch, else the snapshot action's from, else the environment's branch, else master, and must be the same for every deployment that can run the selected test type. A branch mabl does not have is not an error: every test runs at master, and resolved_tests shows it. The snapshot action's from is the exception and must name an existing branch. A test with no version on the branch or master is refused. An environment's snapshot branch has no master fallback, so a test missing from the snapshot is refused. Each enabled test requires a compatible deployment. The first run runs the versions in resolved_tests. Retries, from retry_failed_tests or a manual rerun, resolve the branch again and run any later edit. Flows are not pinned; they resolve on the branch when each test starts.

By default the run stripes across every live personal tunnel the user has (e.g. one per machine); set personal_link_tunnel_label to pin it to one. rerank_with_llm.description:
When true (default), the candidate list is LLM-reranked against the task
description before the top `limit` are returned. When false, the LLM rerank
is skipped and the raw datastore-ordered candidates (ASC by `COSINE_DISTANCE`)
are returned. Either way the response honors `limit`; the internal candidate
widening multiplier varies by endpoint (endpoints that group results after the
fetch keep the widened set so grouping does not underfill `limit`).

EnterTextModeEnum.description:
Application-level preference for how the "enter text" step types into inputs.
Absent means "no preference; runtime falls back to its default."
- `fill`: write the value atomically via Playwright's `fill()`. Fast and reliable for standard inputs.
- `press`: type one character at a time. Slower, but works with autocomplete / per-character event handlers.

TestRecoveryAgentModeEnum.description: Test Recovery Agent mode. Use `inherit` (plan-level only) to defer to the workspace-level default.

RefreshAndRetryFailedStepModeEnum.description: How a plan uses Runtime Recovery Refresh, which reloads the page and re-runs a failed browser step once. `pass` lets the test pass when the re-run passes. `fail_at_end` keeps running from the refreshed page but the step keeps its failure, so the test still fails. `off` never reloads.

PageRefreshRetryOutcomeEnum.description: What happened when Runtime Recovery Refresh reloaded the page and re-ran a failed step. `recovered` means the re-run passed and the step passed with it. `recovered_fail_at_end` means the re-run passed but the plan runs in `fail_at_end` mode, so the step kept its failure. `failed` means the re-run failed too. `reload_failed` means the page could not be reloaded. `cancelled` means the run was stopped before the re-run finished.

step_number.description: The step's display number in the run output, for example `1.3`

PageRefreshRetryStep.description: One step that Runtime Recovery Refresh reloaded the page for during a test run.

recovered_step_count.description: Steps whose re-run passed, in either `pass` or `fail_at_end` mode

PageRefreshRetrySummary.description: Runtime Recovery Refresh outcomes for a test run, written by the execution engine when the run completes. Absent when no step was reloaded.

TraceFidelityEnum.description: How much Chrome trace data to capture. `full` records the complete category set, and is what the "Download step trace" artifact contains. `metrics` records only the categories the published performance measures are computed from, so a trace downloaded from a `metrics` run carries the film strip and timeline but not the full set of Chrome records. `inherit` defers to the next level down.

TraceRetentionEnum.description: Whether the Chrome trace file is kept after a run. `keep` makes it available as the `Download step trace` artifact. `discard` publishes the same performance measures when the analysis succeeds; with no file kept there is no fallback, so a failed analysis loses the measure for that step. A run's `inherit` defers to its plan's setting; a plan's `inherit`, like no setting at all, means `discard`.

bypass_actionability_checks.description:
Application-level preference for whether a click step may act on an element that
fails actionability checks — disabled, hidden, covered, or unstable. Affects new
click steps authored in the test editor or by the Test Creation Agent. `true`
clicks the element anyway; `false` fails the step when the target is not
actionable. Absent means no workspace preference. Per-step overrides set in the
test editor always win.

skip_javascript_fallback_clicks.description:
Application-level preference for whether a click step skips the synthetic
JavaScript fallback click that normally fires when the native browser click
cannot reach the target element — for example when an overlay intercepts the
click or the browser routes the input away from a cross-origin iframe.
`true` fails the step with a clear error instead of clicking synthetically;
`false` or absent allows the fallback (the historical behavior). Newly
created applications default to `true`.

AppModelingRunScopeMode.description:
Which tests a run's work frontier is seeded from.

full: every test that ran against this application in the last 90 days. The default,
and the only mode that also drops de-tagged tests from the frontier and restores
previously deferred ones.

modified_since: the same run-history population, narrowed to tests whose content was
last updated at or after the given timestamp. Intended for incremental knowledge-graph
updates over recently-edited tests.

explicit_tests: exactly the caller-supplied test invariant IDs.

modified_since.description: Required for modified_since, rejected otherwise. Tests whose last update is at or after this instant are seeded.

test_invariant_ids.description: Required for explicit_tests, rejected otherwise. Each ID must name a test that exists in this workspace and is not deleted; unknown IDs fail the request rather than being silently skipped.

AppModelingRunScope.description:
The subset of an application's tests a run covers.

In a scoped mode (modified_since, explicit_tests) the run's scope becomes the frontier's
pending set: the scoped tests are opened for modeling even if an earlier run already
attempted them, tests already attempted outside the scope stay attempted, and tests left
pending by an earlier run that ended early are deferred so this run does not drain them.
A later full run restores deferred tests, so nothing is lost.

Count of distinct plans that ran in the cache window. Derived from distinct plan_id

breakdowns.description:
Ad-hoc per-dimension stat breakdowns keyed by dimension name — the
map stays open for future dimensions (e.g. pass_rate_by_env,
failure_count_by_app, pass_rate_by_browser). Workspace-scope rows
populate, and the RAA workspace reader consumes, these keys:
`top_failing_plans` (array of PlanRunWorkspaceTopFailingPlanEntry),
`top_failing_tests` (array of TestRunWorkspaceTopFailingTestEntry),
`top_failing_plans_exhaustive` / `top_failing_tests_exhaustive` (booleans, present
alongside the corresponding list — see AnalysisCacheSubWindow's fields of the same
name for the exhaustive/sampled semantics),
`sub_windows` (array of AnalysisCacheSubWindow),
`runs_by_day` (array of WorkspaceDayVolumeEntry),
`failure_categories` (object, failure_category_id to failed test run count over the
window, categorized failures only),
`failure_categories_by_day` (array of WorkspaceFailureCategoryDayEntry).

stats-refreshed.

scope_key.description:
Scope identifier — for `test` scope, the test invariant id (e.g.
`abc123-j`). For `plan` scope, the plan id (e.g. `abc123-p`). For
`workspace` scope, the composite
`{app_id or '*'}:{env_id or '*'}`.

AnalysisCacheRefreshTask.description:
Pub/Sub payload (MessageType AI_ANALYSIS_CACHE_REFRESH) instructing the
cache-writer worker to regenerate the LLM-produced narrative
(reference_summary_md) for a specific scope. Stats are refreshed
programmatically by the producer; this task is only the narrative-regen
signal.

test_invariant_id.description: Test invariant id with the `-j` suffix (e.g. `abc123-j`)

test_name.description: Human-readable test name, used for narrative framing

application_id.description: Application id the test most recently ran against, if known

consecutive_failures.description: Count of the most recent consecutive failing runs

failure_category_breakdown.description:
Full-population failure counts keyed by failure category id, computed
over the full cache window.

failure_signatures.description:
Failure-pattern fingerprints computed by the caller over the full
cache window. Surfaced to the model for the narrative; the caller also
persists them on the cache row.

GenerateTestAnalysisCacheRequest.description:
Input to the test-scope cache-writer. The caller (queue-consumer
orchestrator) supplies pre-computed stats and failure signatures (both
derived from the full cache window); the endpoint returns the narrative.

reference_summary_md.description:
Terse, information-dense markdown narrative for the scope. Cap mirrors
AnalysisCache.reference_summary_md.

GenerateAnalysisCacheResponse.description: Cache-writer output — the reference-summary narrative for a cache scope.

scope_key.description:
Workspace composite `{app_id or '*'}:{env_id or '*'}`. v1 is always
`*:*` (whole workspace).

workspace_name.description: Human-readable workspace name, used for narrative framing

coverage_from_time.description: Unix epoch ms — start of the aggregate window

coverage_through_time.description: Unix epoch ms — end of the aggregate window

top_failing_plans.description: Top failing plans over the window, ordered most-failures-first.

top_failing_tests.description: Top failing tests over the window, ordered most-failures-first.

sub_windows.description:
Trailing sub-window pass-rate aggregates (e.g. last_24h vs prior_24h)
so the narrative can frame day-over-day / week-over-week trends.

top_failing_plans_exhaustive.description: True when top_failing_plans was computed from a complete failed-run scan of the window (false means sampled and may misrank).

top_failing_tests_exhaustive.description: True when every failing test in the window contributed to top_failing_tests (false means the list was truncated at the query limit).

GenerateWorkspaceAnalysisCacheRequest.description:
Input to the workspace-scope cache-writer. The caller supplies the
pre-computed workspace plan-run / test-run aggregate (counts, top failing
plans and tests, and trailing sub-window pass rates); the endpoint returns
the narrative. v1 carries no failure signatures.

label.description:
Sub-window label, e.g. `last_24h`, `prior_24h`, `last_7d`, `prior_7d`, `today`,
`yesterday`. `today`/`yesterday` are calendar days in the workspace timezone.

start_time.description: Unix epoch ms — sub-window start

end_time.description: Unix epoch ms — sub-window end

distinct_plans.description: Distinct plans that ran in this sub-window (distinct plan_id across test runs).

distinct_tests.description: Distinct tests (by journey_invariant_id) that ran in this sub-window.

top_failing_plans.description: Top failing plans in this sub-window, ordered most-failures-first. Longer windows only.

top_failing_tests.description: Top failing tests in this sub-window, ordered most-failures-first. Longer windows only.

top_failing_plans_exhaustive.description: True when top_failing_plans was computed from a complete failed-run scan of this sub-window (false means sampled and may misrank).

top_failing_tests_exhaustive.description: True when every failing test in this sub-window contributed to top_failing_tests (false means the list was truncated at the query limit).

AnalysisCacheSubWindow.description:
Aggregate for a sub-window of the cache window. Counts are provided; the writer derives
rates. Rolling windows (last_24h/prior_24h/last_7d/prior_7d) and calendar windows
(today/yesterday, in the workspace timezone) are both expressed here. Distinct counts are
per-window; top-failing lists are populated only on the longer windows (e.g. last_7d).

day.description: Calendar day in the workspace timezone, ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

WorkspaceDayVolumeEntry.description:
Test-run volume for one calendar day (workspace timezone) within the cache window, so the
agent can answer per-day questions like the busiest day by run volume without a tool call.

day.description: Calendar day in the workspace timezone, ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD).

counts.description: Failed test run count keyed by failure_category_id for this day.

WorkspaceFailureCategoryDayEntry.description:
Failed test-run counts by failure category for one calendar day (workspace timezone)
within the cache window, so the agent can answer per-day failure-category questions
without a tool call.

test_run_id.description: The test run ID for which this assertion is being evaluated

assertion_prompt.description: The assertion prompt text to use in evaluating the assertion

assertion_criteria.description: The assertion criteria to use in evaluating the assertion

regenerate_criteria.description: Whether to regenerate the assertion criteria for the assertion (if no criteria are specified, they will always be generated regardless of this setting)

screenshot.description: Base64-encoded screenshot of the element to use in evaluating the assertion

screenshot_mime_type.description: The MIME type of the Base64-encoded screenshot data (optional; defaults to image/png if not provided)

session_id.description: The ID of the current editing session for the assertion, if applicable

test_invariant_id.description: The ID of the test in which this assertion is being evaluated

training_session_id.description: The ID of the current training session for the assertion, if applicable

url.description: The URL on which this assertion is being evaluated

AssertionCriterionVerdict.description: Per-criterion verdict. cannot_verify counts as a failure.

criterion_index.description: Which criterion this verdict is for, as its 1-based position in assertion_criteria. Preferred over the criterion text for attributing a verdict. Optional: when absent the verdict is attributed by matching the criterion text instead.

criterion.description: The criterion this verdict is for

workspace_id.description: The workspace associated with this assertion evaluation

success.description: Whether the assertion was successful (passed) or not (failed)

assertion_criteria.description: The assertion criteria for the assertion, either provided as input or generated during evaluation

explanation.description: The detailed explanation of why the assertion passed or failed

summary.description: The summary of why the assertion passed or failed, if available

criteria_results.description: Per-criterion evaluation results. The assertion passes only when every criterion verdict is met.

data.description: Base64 encoded file data. Mutually exclusive with file_uri - provide exactly one.

file_uri.description: GCS URI of the file (gs://bucket/path format). Mutually exclusive with data - provide exactly one.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file (required for both data and file_uri)

GenAiFileAttachment.description: File attachment for AI evaluation. Exactly one of 'data' or 'file_uri' must be provided.

model_id.description: The model ID to use instead of the default model used by the endpoint

meta_prompt.description: The meta-prompt to use instead of the default used by the endpoint

temperature.description: The temperature to use instead of the default used by the endpoint

test_run_id.description: The ID of the test run to analyze

synopsis.description: The failure synopsis for the analysis

summary.description: The summary of the analysis for the test run failure

plan_run_id.description: The ID of the plan run to analyze

headline.description: The short summary of the plan run analysis; typically limited to one sentence

summary.description: The summary of the plan run analysis

execution_id.description: Identifier of the associated execution for the FailureAnalysis

FailureAnalysisResponse.description: Generative AI failure analysis for an execution

id.description: Analysis ID - may be different when analysis regenerated

workspace_id.description: Owning workspace ID

synopsis.description: A synopsis of the failure summary

summary_text.description: A summary describing the PlanRun failure and potential root cause

prompt_id.description: ID of the prompt used to generate this entity

created_by_id.description: ID of the user who created this entity

created_time.description: Time of entity creation in epoch milliseconds

generated_time.description: Time of successful analysis generation for this entity in epoch milliseconds

agent_session_id.description: ID of the agent session that generated this analysis

evidence_details.description: Agent-generated detailed evidence with visual and technical evidence

content_blocks_json.description: Pre-computed structured content blocks for rich rendering of evidence_details, stored as a JSON array string. Parsed by the UI into ContentBlock[] for rendering.

expire_datetime.description: Date time entity will be automatically purged from storage

dedup_fingerprint_hash.description: SHA-256 of the per-failing-test signature multiset, used by plan-FA dedup.

reused_from_run_id.description: When the failure analysis was reused from a prior run, the ID of the original run that produced the analysis.

analysis_source.description: Who authored this analysis. `auto` is the automatic analysis agent; `user_correction` is a correction a user made in the results chat, which supersedes the automatic reading and is not overwritten by a later automatic analysis of the same execution. Absent on rows written before this field existed, which are automatic.

failing_step_number.description: The step number the run terminally failed at (e.g. "12.4"), from the execution log when the server could determine it, otherwise from the analysis agent. Test-run analyses only.

FailureAnalysis.description: Generative AI failure analysis for a PlanRun

FailureAnalysisSkipReason.description: Why automatic analysis was skipped during a failure burst

skip_reasons.description: Skip reason keyed by entity id; only skipped ids are present.

skipped_test_run_counts.description: For plan run ids in the request: how many of the plan run's test runs had automatic analysis skipped by the burst guard. Only plan runs with at least one are present.

complete.description: False when the lookup could not read every id (for example a cache timeout), so counts may be low.

test_id.description: The invariant ID of the test to analyze

requirement_description.description: The requirement description to compare against. Either this or jira_issue_id must be provided.

jira_issue_id.description: A Jira issue ID to fetch the requirement from. Takes precedence over requirement_description if both are provided.

mabl_branch.description: The mabl branch to read the test's steps from. Defaults to the primary branch.

test_name.description: The name of the analyzed test

requirement_summary.description: A brief summary of the requirement as understood by the analysis

covered_requirements.description: Requirements that are covered by the test steps

coverage_gaps.description: Requirements that are NOT covered by the test steps

summary.description: An overall narrative summary of the coverage analysis

suggestions.description: Suggested test steps or modifications to close coverage gaps

warnings.description: Warnings about issues encountered during analysis (e.g. flows that could not be loaded)

analyzed_test_version.description: The generation number of the test variant whose steps were analyzed. The request names a branch rather than a version, so the analysis reads that branch's head at the moment it runs. A caller that knows which version it meant to grade compares it against this, and treats a mismatch as no verdict rather than recording one about steps it did not write.

analyzed_flow_versions.description: The flow variants that contributed the analyzed steps, in the order they were rendered. The test version alone does not pin the steps: a test references flows by invariant ID and each is resolved at the branch head independently, so the flows can move under an unchanged test version.

invariant_id.description: The invariant ID of the flow that was read

version.description: The generation number of the flow variant that was read

AnalyzedFlowVersion.description: One flow variant read while analyzing a test's coverage.

test_version_id.description: The variant ID of the test version to check, in the form <test invariant ID>:<version> (e.g. abc123-j:7). An invariant ID without a version is rejected.

TestObjectiveAlignmentRequest.description: The test version to check. The check pairs that version's test_objective with that version's own steps, so a verdict names exactly what it judged, unless a draft is given.

objective_summary.description: The objective to check the draft steps against.

steps_text.description: The test's steps as edited, one per line, with steps inside a step group or reusable flow indented beneath it and steps that will not run marked "(disabled)".

TestObjectiveAlignmentDraft.description: Unsaved edits to check instead of the saved version's objective and steps, such as an edit in progress in the trainer. The version named by test_version_id still supplies the test's name and description. The steps arrive already rendered, so the check judges exactly what the editor shows, including unsaved edits inside reusable flows.

summary.description: Why the steps do or do not accomplish the objective. When the verdict is not_aligned, this names what the steps fail to do; when inconclusive, which steps could not be read.

ObjectiveAlignmentVerdict.description: Whether a test's steps accomplish its objective. inconclusive means some of the steps could not be read, so no judgment was made; it must not be recorded as either other verdict.

CoverageGapSeverity.description: How critical a coverage gap is

requirement.description: The specific requirement that is covered

covered_by_steps.description: Which test steps cover this requirement

requirement.description: The specific requirement that is NOT covered

suggestion.description: Suggested approach to close this gap

description.description: The resolved Jira issue description text (summary + description combined)

entity_ids.description: The entities to assess. Each is a mabl test invariant ID (ending in -j), a plan ID (ending in -p), or a deployment event ID (ending in -v). The types may be mixed in a single request; the endpoint resolves each ID to its recent runs. Duplicates are ignored; at most 50 are assessed.

release_context.description: Optional free-text context about the release (e.g. a Jira release ticket summary) that the assessment may weigh when forming its recommendation.

ReleaseReadinessVerdict.description: The overall release readiness recommendation. "pass" = no blocking issues detected; "at_risk" = non-blocking issues or flakiness present; "blocked" = at least one application defect or systemic failure should be resolved before release.

ReleaseReadinessEntityType.description: The kind of entity an ID resolved to.

ReleaseReadinessFailureCategory.description: Whether a failure reflects a real application defect or a test maintenance issue. "application_defect" = a genuine product problem that should block release; "test_implementation" = a test/locator/data issue that does not reflect a product defect.

ReleaseReadinessFailureOnset.description: When a deployment failure began relative to the deployment under assessment, computed from run timestamps. "pre_existing" = the test was already failing before the deployment was received, so this deployment did not cause it; "introduced" = the test passed before the deployment and began failing after it; "unknown" = run history was insufficient to determine onset. Only populated for deployment entities.

entity_id.description: The input entity ID this summary describes

name.description: Human-readable name of the test, plan, or deployment

runs_evaluated.description: Number of recent runs considered for this entity

passed.description: Number of evaluated runs that passed

failed.description: Number of evaluated runs that failed

flaky.description: True when the entity showed intermittent pass/fail across the evaluated runs

stale.description: True when no run occurred in the last 24h and only an older fallback run was available

status.description: Short status description for this entity (e.g. "18/20 passed")

entity_id.description: The input entity ID this failure belongs to

test_name.description: The name of the failing test (or the plan/deployment label when not test-specific)

test_id.description: The id of the failing test, when known

root_cause.description: Root cause drawn from the existing failure analysis for this run

blocking.description: Whether this failure should block the release

onset_evidence.description: Run-history evidence for the onset classification, comparing the failing test's recent run timestamps against the deployment received time

score.description: Overall readiness score from 0 (not ready) to 100 (fully ready)

summary.description: A markdown narrative explaining the recommendation

failures.description: Failure breakdown across all evaluated runs

warnings.description: Issues encountered while gathering data (e.g. entities with no runs, unsupported IDs, runs missing analysis)

entity_id.description: ID of the entity to save analysis on (test run, plan run, or deployment event)

summary.description: Agent-generated analysis summary (root cause + next steps)

content_blocks_json.description: Pre-computed structured content blocks for evidence_details, serialized as a JSON array string. Stored as-is on the FailureAnalysis entity and deserialized by consumers.

agent_session_id.description: ID of the agent session that generated this analysis

reused_from_run_id.description: When the failure analysis was reused from a prior run, the ID of the original run that produced the analysis.

analysis_source.description: Who authored this analysis. Defaults to `auto` (the automatic analysis agent) when absent. `user_correction` marks a correction a user made in the results chat: it is stored as a new analysis attributed to that user, and a later automatic analysis of the same execution will not overwrite it. A correction may omit `evidence_details` and `content_blocks_json`, in which case the evidence already stored for the execution is kept.

failing_step_number.description: The step number the run terminally failed at (e.g. "12.4"), taken from the execution log when the server could determine it, otherwise from the analysis agent. Test-run analyses only.

usage_quantifier.description: The quantifier of the usage associated with this trigger

trigger_time.description: Unix epoch millis when this alert should trigger

AlertTarget.description: An alert target for use with AlertConfiguration and AlertNotification

AlertConfigurationParentNamespace.description: Namespace of the parent to which this AlertConfiguration belongs

parent_id.description: ID of the parent to which this AlertConfiguration belongs

trigger_type.description: Discriminator for the type of trigger for this AlertConfiguration

trigger.description: Configuration of the trigger for this AlertConfiguration. Type depends on trigger_type (AlertConfigurationUsageTrigger for usage, AlertConfigurationTimeBasedTrigger for time_based)

targets.description: Configuration of the targets for this AlertConfiguration

enabled.description: Whether or not this configuration is enabled

created_time.description: Time at which the AlertConfiguration was created

created_by_id.description: The ID of the user who created this AlertConfiguration

last_updated_time.description: Time at which the AlertConfiguration was last updated

last_updated_by_id.description: The ID of the user who last updated this AlertConfiguration

alert_configurations.description: All AlertConfigurations that matched the query

triggered_time.description: Time at which this AlertNotification was triggered

processed_time.description: Time at which this AlertNotification was processed

processed_confirmation_id.description: Confirmation ID from processing the notification, if one exists

processed_time.description: Time at which this AlertNotification was processed

processed_confirmation_id.description: Confirmation ID from processing the notification, if one exists

trigger_id.description: Server-assigned id. The inbox message a firing writes carries it back.

agent_session_id.description: The session this trigger wakes.

entity_id.description: The entity an event trigger watches. For failure_analysis this is the analyzed test run's id.

idempotency_key.description: The key this trigger was stored under, when one was supplied.

registered_by_id.description: The authenticated caller that armed it.

registered_by_agent_session_id.description: The agent session whose credential armed it, when an agent did.

expires_at.description: After this time the trigger never fires.

fire_at.description: For a timer, when it fires. For an event trigger, a fallback: it fires then if the event has not happened.

interval_seconds.description: For a repeating timer, the period between firings until expires_at.

next_execution_target.description: The next time the timer sweep will consider this trigger, when it has a timer.

fired_event_id.description: Identity of the occurrence that fired it.

AgentTrigger.description: A condition that wakes an agent session once. Registered by the session's own agent or by whoever may write the session, and fired by the system, never by a model turn.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the trigger stays armed. Defaults to two hours.

fire_after_seconds.description: Seconds from now until a timer fires, or until an event trigger's fallback fires. Not yet supported; setting it is refused with a 400.

interval_seconds.description: Makes a timer repeat at this period until it expires. Not yet supported; setting it is refused with a 400.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe. The same key on the same session returns the trigger stored the first time.

CreateAgentTriggerRequest.description: An event trigger names entity_type, entity_id and event; a timer names fire_after_seconds or interval_seconds and no entity. An event trigger may add fire_after_seconds as a fallback, so it fires at that time if the event never arrives. Timers and fallbacks are not yet supported: a request setting fire_after_seconds or interval_seconds is refused with a 400.

cursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the next page. Absent on the last page.

agent_session_id.description: The session to wake.

ttl_seconds.description: How long to wait. Defaults to two hours.

NotifyOnComplete.description: Arms a trigger in the same call that starts the work, so the session is woken when the work completes and no completion can land before the trigger exists.

AgentTriggerEventName.description: What happened to the entity. completed applies to plan_run, test_run and failure_analysis; ended, awaiting_input and finalized apply to agent_session. Other pairs are refused.

access_token.description: An external_agent access token acting for the API key.

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires, at most 900 and never past the API key's expiry.

AgentSessionContextAction.description:
What the user did. A closed set, because each member decides what the server does and what it says to the agent — there is no member meaning "something else, here is the text", which is the thing this endpoint exists instead of.
`test_configuration_edited` is the user changing the configuration the agent saved, and is the one action that asks the agent to do something rather than merely telling it something. The four reference actions each name one thing the user pointed the session at. `file_attached` stores the file where the agent can read it by id. `page_viewed` says which page the user is on, which is the one action describing a state rather than an event: it is re-sent when they navigate, and each one replaces the last.

test_id.description: `test_referenced`: the invariant id of the mabl test.

case_identifier.description: `test_case_referenced`: the case as its provider names it — a TestRail case id such as `C1234`, or a Zephyr case key such as `PROJ-T12`. This is what the reading tool takes.

issue_id.description: `xray_test_referenced`: the numeric Jira issue id, which is what Xray's API resolves. Not the key, which nobody but a person uses.

issue_key.description: `xray_test_referenced` and `tracker_issue_referenced`: the key the user picked it by, such as `PROJ-123` or `4815`. For a tracker issue this is what the API reads; for an Xray test it is carried only so the agent can name the test the way the user does.

workspace_integration_id.description: Which integration holds it. Required for every kind but a mabl test: a case id is unique only within one instance and an issue id only within one site, so a reference without this cannot be read — and must never be resolved by trying each integration in turn, which reads whichever one happens to hold that id.

label.description: What the user sees it called. Display only — the agent is told it so it can talk about the thing the way the user does, never so it can look it up.

url.description: Where it lives, when the client knows. Recorded on the reference; not fetched.

AgentSessionContextReference.description: The thing the user pointed the session at. One shape for every kind rather than a variant per action, mirroring the one the clients already use: which fields are read is decided by the action, and a field belonging to another action is ignored rather than refused.

entity_id.description: The id of the thing the page is about, in the form its own tool takes.

label.description: What the page calls it. Display only, so the agent can refer to it the way the user does -- never so it can look it up.

url.description: The page the user is on, when the client knows it. Recorded, never fetched.

AgentSessionContextPage.description:
Where the user is while they talk to the agent, so a workspace-scoped assistant knows which run or deployment "this one" means.
State rather than an event, and the only action here that is: it is re-sent when the user navigates, and each one supersedes the last. That is why it carries the page rather than a change to it, and why the composed message says plainly that it replaces any earlier one.
An entity the agent can already read by id. Nothing is fetched here and nothing is stored on the session: this says what the user is looking at, and the agent reads it with the tool for that kind if it needs to.

AgentSessionContextPageEntity.description: What the page is about. A closed set for the same reason the actions are: each member decides what the server says to the agent, and a member meaning "something else" would put the wording back in the client.

AgentSessionContextCaseProvider.description: Which test case management system `case_identifier` belongs to. Both are read by the same tool, but they are named separately because their identifiers are not interchangeable and the integration behind each resolves differently.

AgentSessionContextTrackerPlatform.description: Which tracker a `tracker_issue_referenced` issue lives in.

id.description: How the agent will name this attachment. Chosen by the caller so that a retry resolves to the file already stored rather than storing a second copy; re-sending an id that this session already holds returns the stored file and writes nothing.

filename.description: What the user calls the file. Shown to the agent and stored as the object's own metadata; nothing is derived from it, and it is not part of where the file lands.

mime_type.description: The file's type, which decides both whether it can be attached at all and how large it may be — a text file is read into the conversation whole, while a PDF reaches the model as media at a fixed cost per page.

content.description: The file itself, base64-encoded. The outer bound here is only what a request body may carry; the ceiling that applies is the one for this file's type, and both it and the per-session totals are enforced on the way in.

AgentSessionContextAttachment.description:
A file the user attached. The bytes ride inline on this request and are written to the workspace's storage before anything is persisted on the session, so raw content never reaches the session row — which is rewritten on every turn, and would therefore be paid for on every turn.
There is deliberately no field for where it is stored. The server mints the location from the session and the id, and the response does not report it: a caller has no way to legitimately know a storage location, so one supplied by a caller would be forged by definition.

test_configuration.description: `test_configuration_edited`: the configuration as the user left it. Sent whole rather than as a description of what moved, because the agent's own tool takes the whole thing and a prose diff would make it reconstruct the object.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe, on the same terms as the inbox: the same key to the same session twice returns the message stored the first time and queues nothing new. The work behind the action is idempotent on its own — a re-sent attachment id resolves to the file already stored under it, and a reference action stores nothing to repeat.

RecordAgentSessionContextActionRequest.description: One thing the user did. Deliberately carries no message text and no storage location: the text is composed by the server from the action and its metadata, which is what keeps model-facing wording versioned with the API rather than written in each client, and the location is minted by the server.

AgentSessionContextConfigurationOrigin.description: Which configuration the user edited, which is the only thing that changes how the edit is put to the agent. `live` is the configuration the conversation is working on. `saved` is a historical snapshot of a configuration the agent already saved, where editing it cannot rewrite anything, so the agent is told to adopt the values rather than that its own working copy moved.

identifier.description: What the agent will call the thing this action named — a test id, a case identifier, the session's own identifier for a tracker issue, or an attachment id. Assigned by the server for a tracker issue, because two issues from different trackers can present the same key and an identifier the agent has already read must never come to mean a different item. Absent for `test_configuration_edited`, which names nothing.

AgentSessionContextActionResult.description: What was queued, and what the agent will know the named thing by.

workspace_id.description: The workspace this instruction belongs to

name.description: A short name or title for the instruction

disabled.description: Whether the instruction is disabled. Disabled instructions are not injected into agent prompts.

test_types.description: Test types this instruction applies to

environment_ids.description: Environment IDs this instruction applies to

application_ids.description: Application IDs this instruction applies to

created_by_id.description: The user who created this instruction

created_time.description: Creation timestamp in epoch milliseconds

last_updated_by_id.description: The user who last updated this instruction

last_updated_time.description: Last update timestamp in epoch milliseconds

AgentInstruction.description: A user-defined instruction that tailors agent behavior for a workspace

workspace_id.description: The workspace to create the instruction in

name.description: A short name or title for the instruction

test_types.description: Test types this instruction applies to

environment_ids.description: Environment IDs this instruction applies to

application_ids.description: Application IDs this instruction applies to

CreateAgentInstructionRequest.description: Request body for creating a new agent instruction

AgentInstructionCapability.description: Capability that an agent instruction applies to

cursor.description: Cursor for fetching the next page of results

AgentInstructionQueryResult.description: Paginated query result for agent instructions

message_index.description: Position in this session's inbox, assigned by the server and dense from zero. Ordering is the point: an agent reads what it was told in the order it was told, and the index is what a cursor moves through.

sender_id.description: The authenticated caller who sent it, never anything the request body said. Recorded so a message can be attributed after the fact.

sender_agent_session_id.description: The agent session this came from, when an agent is speaking. Read off the caller's verified credential rather than the request body, so it attests the topology rather than asserting it. Absent for any other sender.

message.description: What the agent is being told. Bounded because it becomes a permanent turn in a conversation that is re-sent to the model on every turn after it, not merely a request body.

idempotency_key.description: The key this message was stored under, when one was supplied.

created_time.description: Commit time, assigned by the database rather than the caller.

AgentInboxMessage.description: A message queued for an agent. Written by whoever may send to the session, read later by the agent itself. Immutable once stored: the only way to change what an agent was told is to send it something else.

AgentInboxSenderType.description:
Who the message is from, which decides how it reaches the model. `user` is a person, and their text is marked as human authorship. `system` is mabl speaking — a notification, a trigger — and is deliberately NOT marked that way, so an agent is never fed its own machinery back as "what the user asked for". `agent` is another agent session speaking, which names itself in `sender_agent_session_id`.
Derived from the authenticated caller, never sent: a caller with nobody behind it cannot claim a person typed something. An agent's credential names its session, and that is the more specific fact about a caller who is also acting for a person — so a credential naming a session is read as `agent` rather than as the person it acts on behalf of.

AgentInboxSender.description:
How far an agent type opens its inbox. A LEVEL rather than a flag: each one admits everybody the level below it admits, and listed here narrowest first, so a type names one value rather than assembling a set.
`none` admits nobody, which is how a type says it is not reachable. `agent_system` admits the agent sessions belonging to the same orchestrated run — those sharing this session's top-level parent, or being that parent — so a task and its siblings can reach each other without naming one another individually. `session_owner` admits those and whoever created this session. `workspace` admits anyone already authorized to write in the workspace, and so admits everyone.
Every level NARROWS an already-authorized caller; none widens one, and `workspace` is simply the level that narrows by nothing.

context.description: What the user did alongside this message -- attached files, pointed the session at a test, moved to another page. Each is recorded through the context endpoint, in the order given, BEFORE the message is queued, so the api composes the text and queues it as `system`. Sent here rather than as separate calls because every queued message WAKES the agent, this one included: record them afterwards and the agent may answer before they arrive; record them first and the first write wakes it on context with no question in it, and on only part of what was attached. Sent together the agent wakes once, holding all of it. A list rather than one because a single message routinely carries several -- two files, or a file and the page they are about -- and there is no safe way to split those across calls. Carry an `idempotency_key` inside each when you retry, the same as for the message.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe. Sending the same key to the same session twice returns the message stored the first time and queues nothing new — including when the second call carries different text, because the first one is what the agent will act on.

SendAgentInboxMessageRequest.description: A message to queue for an agent, and optionally what the user was doing when they sent it. Everything else — who sent it, whether a person typed it, where it sits in the queue, when it arrived — is derived from the caller or assigned on write, so there is nothing here a caller could get wrong or claim falsely.

TestImpactSessionStartupParams.description: Context for a test impact analysis session. Test impact sessions are written under the server-agents service credential rather than the caller's, so created_by_id identifies the service account and not the requester — the initiating identity is recorded here instead. Trust level: these fields are reported by the service that creates the session, not derived server-side from the authenticated principal, so like every other startup_params field they are only as trustworthy as the credential that wrote the session. Treat them as provenance for internal review, never as an authorization or audit input.

TestImpactInitiatingAuthType.description: The authentication mode of the caller that initiated a test impact analysis. `api_key` callers carry no user identity, so initiating_user_id is expected to be absent for them.

variant.description: The experimental condition this replay ran under (e.g. baseline, no_knowledge_graph). A free-form value on purpose: a new condition is a new value, never a schema change.

replicate.description: 1-based index distinguishing repeated shadow replays of the same original session and variant. Part of the derived idempotency key that keeps a re-run of the same batch window from double-creating a shadow session.

include_plans.description: Whether the replay assumed the original session's plan associations.

TestImpactShadowSessionStartupParams.description: Context for a hidden shadow session that replays a completed test impact analysis session under an experimental variant for internal comparison. Not part of any customer-visible flow; see TestImpactSessionStartupParams for the session being shadowed. application_id, shadow_of_session_id, variant and replicate are required for this session type but are not declared `required` here: the anyOf members flatten into one generated interface, so a required field on one shape becomes required on all of them (see the test_run_id comment on RepairNotesSessionStartupParams below). Enforced by the caller instead.

Provenance only: it records which session's note was in front of the user, never that the user agreed with it, and never an authorization input. Absent on every session not started from a repair note.

CaseLinkIntent.description: One external test case an authoring session links the test it saves to. Server-resolved at session creation; see `case_links`.

application_id.description: The ID of the application being tested

environment_id.description: The ID of the environment being tested

url.description: The URL to start testing from

authoring_mode.description: (Optional) Whether the session authored a new test or started from one that already existed. Derived server-side at session creation from every representation an edit can arrive in (`test_information.test_id`, `test_variant_id`, `agent_state.testInformation.test_id`) and never rewritten, so it records what the session was rather than what its mutable fields say later — `test_id` in particular is rolled forward onto creations at each save. A value supplied by the caller is ignored. Absent on sessions created before it existed, where consumers fall back to inspecting those same fields.

xray_binding_issue_id.description: (Optional) The Jira issue id of the Xray test case this session binds the test it saves to. Resolved server-side at session creation from the references the planning session copied onto this one, and only when the creating caller was authorized to create TCM bindings in this workspace — the binding is provenance the user delegated at creation, so it is frozen here rather than re-read later from a manifest any holder of session write can restate. Never rewritten afterwards, and a value supplied by the caller is ignored. Absent when the caller was unauthorized, when the session references no Xray case or more than one, or when the integration does not belong to this workspace. Meaningless without `xray_binding_integration_id`, which names the Jira site that resolves it.

xray_binding_integration_id.description: (Optional) The Xray workspace integration naming the Jira site that resolves `xray_binding_issue_id`. Resolved server-side at session creation under the same conditions as that field and checked then to belong to this session's workspace; never rewritten, and a value supplied by the caller is ignored. Set and cleared only together with `xray_binding_issue_id`.

case_links.description: (Optional) The external test cases this session links the test it saves to, by adding each `link` to that test's `test_cases`. Resolved server-side at session creation from the references the planning session copied onto this one: at most one per platform, and only when the session references exactly one item of that platform, the creating caller was authorized to edit tests in this workspace, its account has that platform's integration enabled, and the integration is an enabled one of this workspace configured for the case (for Zephyr, its project; for Azure Boards, its organization and project). Never rewritten afterwards, and a value supplied by the caller is ignored. An Azure Boards work item is included only when the tracker reports its category as test case, checked once at creation. Each link's integration and configuration are re-checked when it is written; its category is not.

zephyr_link_case_key.description: DEPRECATED, superseded by `case_links`, and no longer written. On a session created before `case_links` existed, the Zephyr test case key (for example `PROJ-T12`) this session links the test it saves to; still honored when `case_links` is absent. A value supplied by the caller is ignored.

zephyr_link_integration_id.description: DEPRECATED, superseded by `case_links`, and no longer written. The Zephyr workspace integration the case named by `zephyr_link_case_key` was picked from. A value supplied by the caller is ignored.

test_variant_id.description: The variant (version) ID of the test being edited, when this session is an edit of a specific known version. Set in conjunction with `test_information.test_id`.

resume_cursor.description: Optional 1-based-inclusive index of the last saved step the next instance replays before continuing the LLM loop (e.g. "5" replays steps 1–5; absent or "0" replays nothing). Set by the resume planner on continue via `PATCH /agentSession/{id}/startupParams`; not used at session creation.

test_id.description: The invariant id of the test this authoring session operates on. Set at session creation for edits (mirrored from `test_information.test_id`) and rolled forward by the cloud TAA continuation flow at each save/pause via `PATCH /agentSession/{id}/startupParams`, so a resuming instance continues the same test rather than authoring a new one.

branch_id.description: (Optional) The id of the save-to branch — every test and flow version the agent writes lands on it, leaving master untouched. Set once at session creation and mirrored from `test_information.branch_id`; a supplied name is canonicalized to the id, which must resolve inside the session's workspace. An edit session (`test_id` set) that omits it gets a server-created feature branch unless the workspace sets `require_agent_edits_on_branches: false`; creation sessions author on master. Absent on local sessions, which carry the value on `test_information`. A resume reuses it. The branch outlives the session and is closed only by a merge into master (via the branch merge endpoint or `auto_merge`), which is also what flips the session to `merged`.

source_branch_id.description: (Optional) The id of the load-from branch — the branch the agent reads the starting test version from. Mirrored from `test_information.source_branch_id` at session creation. The agent never saves to it (it saves to `branch_id`); when unset, the version loads from master (it does NOT fall back to `branch_id`). Only meaningful for edit sessions.

base_version.description: (Optional) The immutable source-branch version number the edit LOADED FROM — the variant of the `source_branch_id` branch (or master, when unset) at the moment the runtime fetched the starting test. Written once by the runtime at initial load and never rolled forward, so it pins the "Review changes" diff baseline to the version actually edited rather than the source branch's current tip (which can advance while the edit is in flight). Only meaningful for edit sessions; absent on older sessions, where consumers fall back to the source branch's current version tag.

auto_merge.description: When true, the session's `branch_id` is merged into master on a successful session completion (provided the branch still resolves to this workspace and has new versions). Defaults to absent/false — the branch is left open for human review.

repair_notes_session_id.description: The runtime repair notes session whose finding seeded this edit

impact_session_id.description: (Optional) The test impact analysis session this session answers — the reverse half of the link whose forward half is a remote artifact of kind `AgentSession` on that impact session. Like every other startup_params field it is only as trustworthy as the credential that wrote the session. On an authoring session it is provenance only: nothing is granted by it and nothing dereferences it. The initiate endpoint (`initiateTestAuthoringSession`) checks that it exists, is in the same workspace and is a `test_impact` session; this generic create path does not, so a session written directly here can carry an unchecked value. An `exploratory_qa` session that started from an analysis explores that session's change; its initiate endpoint (`initiateExploratoryQaSession`) runs the same checks and also requires the analysis to have finished. Deliberately NOT `parent_session_id`, which on this path means the planning session whose artifacts are copied into this one.

AgentInstanceStatus.description: The status of the latest agent instance driving a session. The same enum is used for cloud and local instances. Cloud-only values (`queued`, `terminating`, `rate_limited`, `skipped`) are set by the cloud instance lifecycle (start/terminate/end). Common values (`running`, `needs_attention`, `completed`, `failed`, `terminated`) are written by either cloud or local clients. `merged` is a session-level state applied after a `completed` authoring task's branch is merged into master (via the branch merge endpoint or the session's `auto_merge` setting); the underlying cloud instance stays `completed`. `accepted` and `closed` are session-level review outcomes for a finished authoring task, set only through the review endpoint; the underlying cloud instance keeps its own status. `accepted` records that the user kept the authored test. `closed` records that the user discarded it; the session's test is left in place unless the caller asked for it to be deleted (`delete_test` on the review request), no branch is deleted either way, and the session's conversation is retained so the task can be regenerated from it. Both are terminal in the same sense as `merged` — neither is resumable, and no lifecycle transition leaves them. `resuming` is a transient, server-set-only state on the session (no instance holds it) — the cloud TAA continuation flow flips a resumable session to `resuming` while it plans the answer, then to `queued` when the new instance spawns (or back to a resumable status on re-clarification, or `failed` on error). It is the concurrency guard, so a second answer to a `resuming` session is rejected. The session's `instance_type` field indicates which kind of instance owns the session. Use `none` in query parameters to match sessions without any status.

AgentInstanceType.description: Indicates what kind of agent instance is driving a session. `cloud` means a server-managed cloud instance owns the lifecycle (created via the cloudInstance endpoints). `local` means a local client (e.g. mabl CLI) is driving the session via updateAgentSession.

AgentCloudInstanceTerminationReason.description: The reason for terminating a cloud instance. 'infra_shutdown' covers any shutdown signal from the runtime environment (K8s pod eviction, Cloud Run instance cycling, etc.) — kept generic so it applies regardless of where the agent runs. 'dispatch_failed' means the instance never started — its start message failed to publish, or expired in the queue before any runner claimed it. 'agent_stalled' means the agent was still alive but stopped making progress, so a watchdog hard-killed it. 'agent_error' means the agent threw or exited unexpectedly while its work was still in flight.

When the label is a test run id or other opaque identifier, authors SHOULD supply the full value from tool output; dashboard clients SHOULD render it without truncation (e.g. no ellipsis) so users can match listings and copy ids.

url.description: Resolver target for the client. Google Cloud Storage links (https, virtual-hosted, `gs://`, or scheme-less `storage.googleapis.com/...` in markdown) are normalized to `gs://bucket/object`. Other targets stay as authored (typically `https://...` app or docs URLs).
