reference_ids.description: Optional identifiers parsed from the link target (UUIDs, execution path segments, etc.). Clients may map these to workspace routes or entity lookups; artifact download still uses `url` with `getArtifactUrl` when `url` is `gs://...`.

DashboardLinkHint.description: Structured navigation target derived from a text block: markdown `[label](url)` links, **naked** `gs://bucket/object` strings (e.g. in table cells, not wrapped in markdown links), and opaque mabl workspace entity ids whose **type suffix** is `-jr` (test run), `-pr` (plan run), `-v` (deployment), `-p` (plan), `-j` (test), `-f` (flow), `-a` (application), or `-e` (environment) when `workspace_id` was supplied on the convert request (path-only app routes under `/workspaces/{id}/...`). Presence in `link_hints` means the client should offer guarded navigation (preview / confirmation) before leaving the analysis view. Google Cloud Storage targets are normalized to canonical `gs://` for `getArtifactUrl` like typed `screenshot` / `har` blocks. Optional `reference_ids` carries parsed path tokens or entity ids for in-app linking.

link_hints.description: Optional structured link metadata: markdown `[label](url)` (http(s), `gs://`, scheme-less GCS hosts), naked `gs://...` outside markdown links, and opaque mabl entity ids (type suffix `-jr`, `-pr`, `-v`, `-p`, `-j`, `-f`, `-a`, `-e`) when `workspace_id` was provided. Google Cloud Storage targets normalize to `gs://` for signing. Same order as first-seen distinct `url` after deduplication. Empty or omitted when there are no such links.

TextBlock.description: Markdown text for fallback or narrative. When artifact URIs are not represented as typed blocks (`screenshot`, `har`, …), authors should use `[label](url)` with `https://`, `storage.googleapis.com/...`, or `gs://` hrefs instead of naked paths in table cells; those links are surfaced in `link_hints` for guarded client navigation. The conversion pipeline strips redundant bare repeats of a URI that already appears in a preceding `screenshot` or `har` block, but preserves normal markdown links.

artifact_uri.description: URI of the screenshot artifact (`gs://` preferred; HTTPS GCS URLs may be normalized server-side)

label.description: Optional label for the screenshot

ScreenshotBlock.description: Primary dashboard representation for an image/screenshot artifact. Clients MUST render this block (not the raw `artifact_uri` string elsewhere) as the main image channel. Optional `label` and `caption` carry human-readable context; do not duplicate the same `artifact_uri` as bare prose or filler table rows in sibling text when this block is present — use a markdown link only if a separate “open elsewhere” affordance is intentional.

segments.description: The data segments of the chart

x_axis_label.description: Optional label for the category axis (often the table's label column header). Clients should show this near the axis; include units on the value axis via `y_axis_label` when the metric is not obvious from the title alone.

y_axis_label.description: Optional label for the numeric axis (often the table's value column header). Use this to convey units and scale — e.g. `Duration (ms)`, `Count`, `Pass rate (%)` — especially when segment values are raw numbers.

BarChartBlock.description: A content block displaying a bar chart

segments.description: The data points of the chart, one per (label, series) pair

x_axis_label.description: Optional label for the category (x) axis, often the table's label column header.

y_axis_label.description: Optional label for the numeric (y) axis; use it to convey units and scale.

LineChartBlock.description: A content block displaying a line chart. Segments share the `BarChartSegment` shape: `label` is the x-axis category (usually a date or time bucket), `series` names the line, `value` is the y value.

PieChartBlock.description: A content block displaying a pie chart. Each segment is one slice: `label` names it and `value` is its size; slices are shown as proportions of the total.

payload.description: JSON payload for the Datatron renderer (e.g. spec, bindings, or chart configuration). The analysis dashboard may emit view `label_count` with `segments: [{ label, value, color }]` when converting label+count markdown tables (same table shape as bar charts, different annotation). Per-segment `color` uses `DashboardChartColorToken` (semantic keys), same as `BarChartSegment.color`, for theme-aware rendering on the client. The server normalizes segments so `color` is always set: Passed / Failed / Stopped / Terminated* use semantic tokens; other rows alternate `purple` and `teal`.

DatatronBlock.description: Embedded Datatron visualization or data view (payload interpreted by the Datatron client)

artifact_uri.description: URI of the HAR file (gs:// or https), same pattern as screenshot blocks

har.description: Inline W3C HAR JSON when the HAR is embedded instead of linked

label.description: Optional label for the HAR viewer chrome

HarBlock.description: Primary dashboard representation for a HAR / network trace (and parity pattern for similar file-backed network artifacts). Exactly one of `artifact_uri` (linked HAR file) or `har` (inline W3C document with `log.entries`) SHOULD be set for a meaningful viewer; do not treat prose or markdown tables as the canonical copy when this block carries the real artifact. Prefer this typed block over markdown tables with an “Artifact URI” column full of bare paths. DOM snapshots, variables JSON, and other structured payloads SHOULD use dedicated typed blocks or `datatron` / `log_lines` as the contract evolves — not duplicate channels (e.g. empty `har` block plus full trace only in text).

LogLinesBlock.description: Structured log lines for dedicated log rendering (levels, sources). Prefer this (or `har` / `datatron`) over markdown tables whose cells are only bare artifact URIs without typed blocks.

column_weights.description: Optional relative widths for CSS grid/flex (e.g. 1, 2, 1); client normalizes

ColumnsBlock.description: Multi-column layout for side-by-side summaries, comparisons, or mixed block types

ContentBlock.description: Discriminated union of dashboard blocks. The conversion service aims for one canonical typed block per artifact URI (or inline payload): screenshots as `screenshot`, traces/HAR as `har`, console-style output as `log_lines`, structured metrics as `datatron`, `bar_chart`, `line_chart` or `pie_chart`, etc. Text blocks carry narrative and markdown links; they should not re-list the same storage URI as the only content when a typed block already references it (markdown `[label](uri)` links remain for optional secondary navigation).

cloud_agent_instance_id.description: The ID of the cloud instance

triggered_by_message_id.description: The message ID that triggered this instance to start

agent_type.description: The type of agent being run on the cloud instance

machine_config.description: Configuration details for the cloud machine

entity_id.description: The ID of the referenced entity

entity_name.description: The name of the referenced entity

metadata.description: (Optional) Free-form string-to-string detail about WHY this entity is attached to the session — e.g. `relation`, `revision`, `source`, `url` on a deployment event an analysis triggered. `relation` reads outward from the session: `triggered` (this session's analysis caused that deployment event), `spawned` (this session started that session), `reported` (that test run reported back to this session). `source` names who or what put the entity there, and it answers a slightly different question per relation, so read it with its relation rather than as one vocabulary: on a `triggered` deployment event it is the `TestSelection.source` that chose the tests (`agent` or `user`); on a `triggered` plan run it is who dispatched the batch (`agent`); on a `reported` test run it is where the run happened (`mabl_local`); on a `spawned` authoring session it is the client that wrote the link (`agent` from the MCP tools, `mabl_cli_authoring` from the CLI). A new writer joins the value space its relation already uses rather than opening another one. Both are conventions, not validated enums. Values are strings so the Datastore/Spanner JSON round trip stays unambiguous and nothing structured hides behind an untyped map. A remote artifact's identity is `entity_kind` + `entity_id` and a re-write of the same pair replaces the whole artifact (last write wins), so `metadata` must never be the only carrier of something that matters.

ArtifactEntityKind.description: The kind of entity that a remote artifact references. PascalCase: TypeScript consumers compare these values literally.

workspace_id.description: The ID of the workspace in which to create the session

parent_session_id.description: The ID of the parent agent session, if any. An agent's new session always has the calling agent's session as its parent, so an agent may only omit this or send its own session; an external agent, which acts with no session, may not send one; a person or API key may name any session they can read.

messages.description: Initial messages in the agent session

initiating_request_id.description: A unique identifier for the request that initiated this agent session. If set, this must be globally unique and requests to create a new agent session with the same initiating_request_id will fail.

related_artifacts.description: Artifacts related to this agent session. Written as given — creation is the one path that does not merge, because there is nothing yet to merge with.

notify_on_complete.description: Wakes the parent session when this session ends. Requires parent_session_id, and its agent_session_id must name that parent.

CreateAgentSessionRequest.description: Request to create a new agent session

related_artifacts.description: Artifacts related to this agent session. MERGED into the session's existing artifacts, not substituted for them: inline artifacts dedupe by `name`, remote artifacts by `entity_kind` + `entity_id`, and the ones in this request win on a collision. Omit the field entirely to leave the session's artifacts untouched. To attach artifacts without a message, use `POST /agentSession/{id}/artifacts` instead.

AppendAgentSessionMessageRequest.description: Request to append a message to an agent session

messages.description: The messages to upsert in the session

related_artifacts.description: Artifacts related to this agent session. MERGED into the session's existing artifacts, not substituted for them: inline artifacts dedupe by `name`, remote artifacts by `entity_kind` + `entity_id`, and the ones in this request win on a collision. Omit the field entirely to leave the session's artifacts untouched. To attach artifacts without a message, use `POST /agentSession/{id}/artifacts` instead.

inbox_cursor_through.description: Advance the session's inbox cursor past this `message_index`, in the SAME transaction as this message write. The caller has already put those messages into the conversation it is writing, so consuming them and recording the turn that consumed them commit together or not at all. A message that arrived after the caller read has a higher index and is left for the next turn. A session with no inbox is not an error — nothing is advanced.

UpsertAgentSessionMessagesRequest.description: Request to upsert messages in an agent session. Messages are matched by ID - new messages are inserted, existing messages are updated.

related_artifacts.description: The artifacts to attach. MERGED into the session's existing artifacts: inline artifacts dedupe by `name`, remote artifacts by `entity_kind` + `entity_id`, and the ones in this request win on a collision, so re-sending one is idempotent and nothing already on the session is dropped.

UpsertAgentSessionArtifactsRequest.description: Request to attach artifacts to an agent session without writing a message. Object-wrapped rather than a bare array because Swagger Inflector cannot bind a top-level array of a polymorphic schema to its generated model and degrades it to raw JSON nodes.

related_artifacts.description: The session's complete artifact list after the merge.

warning.description: Present when the write succeeded but did not store everything it was sent — today, only when the session is already at its related-artifact limit, where excess incoming artifacts are dropped rather than failing a write that may also carry messages.

AgentSessionArtifacts.description: An agent session's artifacts, without the rest of the session.

impersonate_user_id.description: The ID of the user that the cloud instance should impersonate when running. Defaults to the launching person; the stored value is the person the instance acts for, or empty when it acts as the workspace agent user.

impersonated_principal_is_support_admin.description: Set by the server, ignored on input. True when the instance acts for a support admin who is not a member of the workspace.

launch_principal_resolved.description: Set by the server, ignored on input. True when impersonate_user_id holds the resolved principal the instance acts for rather than the requested target.

launch_principal_api_key_id.description: Set by the server, ignored on input. The API key the instance acts for when it was started with a key and no person, in which case impersonate_user_id is empty.

snapshot.description: Optional. A specific snapshot Docker image tag — the commit SHA of a published agent build — to launch this agent type from instead of its standard deployed image. Used to exercise a pre-release/preview build within a session. Leave unset to use the agent type's normal deployed image.

api_image.description: Optional. A mabl API deploy-preview tag (e.g. `dp-my-branch`) that routes the launched cloud agent's own API calls through `https://<tag>.api-preview.mabl.com` instead of the standard API. Used to exercise API changes end-to-end within an authoring session. Non-prod, cloud-mode only. Leave unset to use the standard API.

resume_attempt_id.description: Optional. The resume attempt id (the resume cycle's user_message_id). When present, the create transaction atomically binds this attempt's resume_payload_<cycle> artifact to the new instance (spawn_resolution='spawned' plus spawned_instance_id) in the same commit that creates the instance and flips the session status. Test-authoring resume spawns only; ignored otherwise.

CreateAgentCloudInstanceRequest.description: Request to create a new cloud instance

TerminalAgentInstanceStatus.description: Statuses an instance can transition to as it stops doing work. Terminal for the pod (which exits and releases its quota slot); whether the task can continue is tracked separately. 'skipped' signals that the agent chose not to do work (e.g., a dedupe gate matched) and is distinct from 'terminated' which signals an interruption. 'needs_attention' signals the agent paused on a user-input request (execute_ask_for_help) — the pod stops but the session remains continuable.

EndAgentCloudInstanceRequest.description: Request to end a cloud instance with a terminal status

LocalSettableAgentInstanceStatus.description: AgentInstanceStatus values that local clients (e.g. mabl CLI) can write via updateAgentSession. Subset of AgentInstanceStatus that excludes cloud-orchestration values (`queued`, `terminating`, `rate_limited`, `skipped`) which are managed by the cloud instance lifecycle, not by local clients.

AgentSessionReviewOutcome.description: What the user decided about a finished authoring task. `accepted` keeps the authored work; `closed` discards the task. Neither deletes anything on its own; a caller closing a task can additionally ask for its test to be deleted via `delete_test`. Both are terminal session-level statuses — see AgentInstanceStatus, whose values these mirror.

outcome.description: The decision to record. The session ends in the matching status.

delete_test.description: (Optional) Delete the test this session saved, as part of closing it. Valid only with the `closed` outcome; sending it with `accepted` is a 400. The caller must hold write access to journeys in the session's workspace, the same permission deleting the test directly would need. The test is identified from the session (`startup_params.test_id`, else its one remote `Test` artifact) rather than named by the caller, and only a test the session itself authored is deletable — established from `authoring_mode` and from the test having been created after the session began, either of which refusing on its own. A session with no saved test, several with nothing to single one out, or one it did not author, and a test that cannot be deleted, are each a 409 with nothing closed — as is the session itself changing between the target being resolved and the close. The TEST is deliberately not version-pinned: a concurrent edit to it does not block the deletion, which removes the test rather than a particular version of it. Nothing else is deleted — flows cascade as they do for any test deletion, and the branch is untouched.

ReviewAgentSessionRequest.description: Request to record a review outcome on a finished authoring session

UpdateAgentSessionRequest.description: Partial-update request for an agent session. All fields are optional; only fields present in the body are updated.

resume_cursor.description: 1-based-inclusive index of the last saved step to replay before the resumed instance continues (absent or "0" replays nothing). Set by the resume planner on continue.

test_id.description: The invariant id of the test the session operates on. Set by the resume flow at pause (and at each save) so the next instance continues the same test.

url.description: The URL the next instance should boot against (the pausing pod's most recent URL).

application_id.description: Refined application id if the pausing pod resolved a previously-unknown application.

environment_id.description: Refined environment id if the pausing pod resolved a previously-unknown environment.

branch_id.description: The id of the branch the agent operates on. Lifecycle is documented on `TestAuthoringSessionStartupParams.branch_id`.

base_version.description: The source-branch version the edit actually LOADED FROM, reported by the runtime once at initial load (see `TestAuthoringSessionStartupParams.base_version`). This is the server-computed `entity_version` the load returned, not a value the caller derives. Write-once and validated: it is stored only when the session has no `base_version` yet and the supplied version is >= 0 (versions are zero-indexed, so 0 is a valid initial-version baseline; a negative sentinel is dropped). A later pause/save that re-sends it (or a newer value) is ignored, so the baseline can never drift off the loaded version.

auto_merge.description: Whether the session's branch should be auto-merged into master on clean completion.

UpdateAgentSessionStartupParamsRequest.description: Partial update of the resumable subset of an agent session's `startup_params` field, used by the cloud TAA continuation flow to roll the session's "latest used / next to be used" authoring context forward. All fields are optional; only fields present in the body are written. Creation-attribution fields on the underlying `startup_params` (`agent_session_source`, `test_variant_id`) and the polymorphic discriminator (`type`) are preserved unchanged — this endpoint is NOT a full partial-update of the `startup_params` JSON object.

credentials_id.description: The id of the credential to bind for the resumed session (an id only — the secret is resolved + pre-fetched by the pod, never stored here).

datatable_id.description: The id of the data table for data-driven steps.

scenario_id.description: The id of the scenario (a named row) within the data table. Must belong to the effective data table — the setter rejects an incoherent pair.

url_override.description: The base/start URL the resumed session should use (kept coherent with the top-level `url`).

application_id.description: The application id (kept coherent with the top-level `application_id`).

environment_id.description: The environment id (kept coherent with the top-level `environment_id`).

ResumableTestInformationUpdates.description: The allowlisted subset of `agent_state.testInformation` that the cloud TAA resume flow may merge field-by-field. Security-reviewed: these are the only nested fields the startup-params setter will write. References/ids only — never secret values. Keep in sync with `RESUMABLE_TEST_INFORMATION_FIELDS` in `AgentSessionServiceImpl`.

test_run_metrics.description: Test run counts by status across every deployment event in deployment_event_ids, counted the same way as a deployment event result's run_result.journey_execution_metrics, retries included, so an event that also matched plans by label counts those plans' runs too. All zero when no tests have run.

request.description: The request as the analysis ran it, after validation and normalization. Absent until the analysis returns, and on a session whose recorded request cannot be read or no longer matches this schema.

result.description: The result as stored on the session. For a caller who can read the workspace's agent sessions, each test carries the run_context stored with it, facts as of when they were stored rather than re-read. A key holding only read:test_impact_analyses gets each test without it, and quality_window and run_context_incomplete then describe run context this read leaves out. A test whose stored run_context no longer matches its schema comes back without it, the rest of the result kept, and run_context_incomplete is then true. Absent until the analysis returns, and on a session whose stored result cannot be read or no longer matches this schema, as a result stored before a property became required does.

reference_key.description: The normalized type:id key that groups analyses of this reference. Pass it as reference to queryTestImpactSessions to list every analysis of this reference.

TestImpactReference.description: One change reference and the newest live test impact analysis that names it

summary.description: Unstructured summary text describing the review findings

structured_summary.description: Structured JSON summary as a string (JSON format defined by the system prompt)

AgentReviewSummary.description: Summary output from an agent review session containing both unstructured and structured review findings

fullStepList.description:
DEPRECATED. Array of step descriptions representing all steps in the test. Each string is a human-readable description of a test step.
Prefer formatted_steps, which carries authoritative dot-notation path indices and step IDs from the runtime.
Retained as a required field for backwards-compatibility with older clients that have not yet upgraded to emit formatted_steps.

cursorPosition.description:
DEPRECATED. Index where new steps will be inserted (cursor position). Steps before this index have been executed.
Prefer cursor_path, which carries the dot-notation path of the entry the cursor sits before.
Retained as a required field for backwards-compatibility with older clients.

currentTaskIndex.description: Index of the current task from TestCreationOutline.tasks that is being executed.

variables.description: Variables created during test execution. Key is variable name, value is the variable value.

lastTaskStatus.description: Results of the last actions that were executed. Used to determine which steps are deletable (can be undone).

formatted_steps.description:
Pre-formatted step entries with authoritative dot-notation paths and (optional) step IDs.
Emitted by upgraded clients (mabl-cli) that compute the indices from the canonical step tree rather than inferring them from text.
When present, the api renders this directly and ignores fullStepList. When absent, the api falls back to legacy text-based formatting of fullStepList.

cursor_path.description:
Dot-notation path of the entry the cursor sits immediately before (e.g. "2.3"). An empty string indicates the cursor is at the end of the test.
Paired with formatted_steps. When formatted_steps is absent, cursorPosition is used instead.

TestExecutionState.description: Tracks the current position and state of test execution. This artifact is updated as the agent creates steps and moves through tasks.

path.description:
Dot-notation position label for this entry (e.g. "1", "2.3", "2.3.1"). For end-of-group/flow entries this MAY be empty,
since end markers do not occupy their own addressable position. The number of dotted segments encodes nesting depth
(e.g. "2.3.1" is depth 2), so consumers can derive layout from path alone without a separate indent field.

text.description:
Human-readable step text. For step entries this is the rendered step description (e.g. "Click Submit").
For task or flow start/end entries this is the group or flow name (without any "Start task:" / "End execute flow:" prefix).

kind.description:
What kind of entry this is. Drives how the api renders the line:
- step: a leaf step inside the test
- task-start / task-end: opening / closing marker for a step group
- flow-start / flow-end: opening / closing marker for a flow boundary

step_id.description:
Stable canonical step identifier from the client's step tree. Used by tools that prefer step_id over positional indices.
Populated for step entries and for the start marker of a step group / flow (task-start / flow-start carry the wrapping
step's id). End markers (task-end / flow-end) and legacy step-tree fragments without IDs have no addressable step_id
and omit this field.

flow_id.description:
Invariant ID of the saved reusable flow a flow-start marker opens. Present only when the flow exists as its own
entity, so its body can be fetched by ID; absent for a flow defined inside the test and for every other kind.

collapsed_step_count.description:
Number of steps in this flow's body that were left out of the list. Present only on a flow-start marker whose body
was omitted, and only when the count is known, so its presence is what distinguishes a collapsed flow from an empty
one. The omitted steps belong to the flow entity, not to the test, and are read back with the flow's ID. A body
with nothing in it is never omitted - that flow is empty, which the absent count already says - so the count is
at least one.

FormattedStep.description:
A single pre-formatted step entry computed by the client from the canonical step tree.
Used inside TestExecutionState.formatted_steps to render the step list with authoritative dot-notation paths.

Unset means shadow.

publish_time.description: The time the message was published

healthy_count.description: The number of health checks that passed

unhealthy_count.description: The number of health checks that failed

checks.description: The status of each check that was performed

health_check_name.description: The name of the health check that was performed

is_healthy.description: True if this individual check reported healthy; false otherwise

message.description: The message returned by the health check

count.description: Number of items returned in this response, maybe 0 if count == limit on last call

cursor.description: Cursor that can be used to fetch the next page, count <= limit

error_code.description: Machine-readable reason for the error, present only when the API names one. Values are guardrail_blocked (a guardrail policy refused an agent request), approval_required (a guardrail policy requires a person to approve the request first).

guardrail.description: The guardrail policy that refused the request; present only when error_code is guardrail_blocked or approval_required.

id.description: The id of the guardrail policy that decided the refusal.

reason.description: Why the policy refuses the request, written for the person the agent acts for.

decision_id.description: The id of this decision in the guardrail decision log.

action.description: The action the request was evaluated as, written Verb::Resource (for example Delete::Test), as declared by the operation's x-mabl-action extension.

policy_source.description: Who set the deciding policy: workspace for a rule the workspace's owners wrote, account for a rule set for the workspace's account, mabl_agent_type for the agent type's ceiling, and mabl_default for mabl's own defaults.

approval.description: The approval for this request; present when error_code is approval_required and the approval could be recorded. Without it the request cannot be approved.

GuardrailRefusal.description: The guardrail policy that refused an agent request.

request_expires_time.description: When the approval expires if nobody decides it, in epoch milliseconds.

url.description: The mabl app page where a person reviews the approval.

GuardrailApprovalRef.description: An approval a guardrail policy asks for. While it is PENDING, stop: give the person the url, tell them the request is waiting for approval, and do not repeat the request or poll in a loop. Once a person tells you it is APPROVED, repeat the identical request with the header X-Mabl-Approval set to id. DENIED means a person said no, so do not work around it.

GuardrailApprovalState.description: Where a guardrail approval stands. PENDING awaits a decision and expires undecided after 24 hours; APPROVED lets the agent repeat the request, as often as it does, for 20 minutes; DENIED refuses the same request for 20 minutes after the decision, after which asking again opens a new approval; CANCELLED means a person withdrew it while pending or revoked it while approved. EXPIRED and CANCELLED are final.

GuardrailApprovalKind.description: Who decides a guardrail approval. SELF is decided by the person the agent acts for; WORKSPACE, for an agent acting for an API key, by a workspace owner or editor.

type.description: The kind of thing the reference names, which decides how mabl normalizes the id.

id.description: The identifier in the owning system, e.g. "github.com/mablhq/ui#3341", "9f2c1ab", "MABL-21839". For a pull_request the host is part of the canonical key, so a hostless id such as "mablhq/ui#3341" is a different reference from "github.com/mablhq/ui#3341" and the two never group together; supply the pull request url, either here or in url, and mabl derives the host-qualified form. Required unless url is given and parseable. Whitespace and the characters < > " are rejected, as is a backslash: url parsers read one as a path separator, so a value carrying it names a different thing than it reads as.

url.description: Optional link. Rendered, never parsed for meaning, except to derive the canonical id for a pull_request. When both are given and both name a pull request, they must name the same one. Held to http or https, and rejected for whitespace, < > " or a backslash - a backslash is a path separator to a url parser and an ordinary character to a reader, so one url would name two hosts.

title.description: The pull request title. On the test impact reads (queryTestImpactSessions, getTestImpactAnalysis and queryTestImpactReferences), mabl sets it from the source control of a linked deployment event that lists this pull request, and leaves it absent when no such event is known or the reference is not a pull request. On those reads the session's references and each reference row carry this value in place of any title sent on input.

ChangeReference.description: A reference to the change an analysis is about, in the system that owns it. Supply every reference you know (a pull request and the ticket it closes, for example): the more references an analysis carries, the more views it appears in. Normalized by mabl before it is stored.

task_name.description: The "short" name of the task, or, if no name was specified at creation, a unique system-generated id.

task_retry_count.description:
The number of times this task has been retried. For the first attempt, this value is 0.
This number includes attempts where the task failed due to 5XX error codes and never reached the execution phase.

task_execution_count.description:
The total number of times that the task has received a response from the handler.
Since Cloud Tasks deletes the task once a successful response has been received, all previous handler responses were failures.
This number does not include failures due to 5XX error codes.

task_eta.description: The schedule time of the task in seconds since January 1st 1970, specified as a decimal number.

task_previous_response.description: The HTTP response code from the previous retry.

task_retry_reason.description: The reason for retrying the task.

ErrorResponse409.description: Conflicts with the current state of the resource
